The 2026 Urban Local Body elections were held recently in Rajasthan for 309 urban local bodies and 10,244 wards, with polling held on 09 and 11 September and counting on 14 September. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won 4,182 wards, followed by the Congress with 3,619, while Independents secured 2,273 wards. The results also saw the BJP secure majorities in several municipal corporations, while Congress and Independent candidates won in some others (here, here).
In this context, a video is circulating on social media (here, here, and here), claiming it shows a BJP candidate crying after receiving just one vote in the Rajasthan civic elections. The post also alleges that even his own family members did not vote for him. Let’s verify the claim made in the post in this article.
Claim: The video shows a BJP candidate crying after receiving just one vote in the 2026 Rajasthan civic elections.
Fact: It is true that a BJP candidate named Kailash Chandra received one vote in the 2026 Rajasthan civic elections. However, the viral video is unrelated to this incident. The man seen in the video is Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Shivchandra Ram, who was seen crying during a press conference in June 2026 after being denied an MLC ticket in Bihar. Hence, the claim made in the post is Misleading.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to several media reports (here, here, here, and here) published in June 2026 featuring the same video. According to these reports, the person seen crying during a press conference is RJD leader and former Bihar minister Shivchandra Ram, who broke down in tears after being denied an MLC ticket. RJD’s Sunil Singh had filed the nomination for the Grand Alliance for one of the 10 seats in the Bihar Legislative Council, which reportedly angered Ram. He alleged that the party had promised to make him an MLC but had betrayed him, following which he announced his resignation from all RJD posts, while clarifying that he had not left the party. This confirms that the viral video is unrelated to the 2026 Rajasthan civic elections.
To investigate the claim that a BJP candidate received only one vote in the 2026 Rajasthan civic elections, we conducted a Google keyword search and found multiple reports (here, here). According to these reports, BJP candidate Kailash Chandra received only one vote in Ward No. 13 of the Parbatsar Municipality in Rajasthan’s Deedwana-Kuchaman district. Congress candidate Hina Khanam received 376 votes, while Independent candidate Rasheed Khan received 195 votes. The reports also state that Kailash Chandra was a voter in Ward No. 12 but was fielded by the BJP from Ward No. 13, meaning he could not vote for himself.
We then checked the election results available on the official website of the Rajasthan State Election Commission. The results for the Parbatsar Municipality show that Kailash Chandra, the BJP candidate from Ward No. 13, received one vote.
To sum up, an unrelated video of a Bihar RJD leader crying is falsely linked to the BJP candidate who received one vote in the 2026 Rajasthan civic polls.

Five baby orangutans have been found in a forest in India, prompting authorities to investigate if they were trafficked into the country from south-east Asia.
The orangutans, native only to the islands of Borneo and Sumatra and known for their shaggy red fur, were found in Balasore district of Odisha state, thousands of kilometres away from their natural habitat.
Odisha’s environment minister, Ram Singh Khuntia, said wildlife investigators were trying to establish how the rare apes reached India.
“We suspect that an international racket might be involved in this,” Singh said.
International commercial trade in orangutans is prohibited under Cites – a global agreement governing trade in endangered wildlife.
The five babies were found by forest department officials who were patrolling in the Jaleswar range in Balasore district.
Officials believed the orangutans had been in the area for just a few days, and they have now been placed in quarantine at a zoological park in Odisha.
According to the World Wildlife Fund, about 104,000 orangutans remain in Borneo and Sumatra, down from more than 230,000 a century ago.
The Tapanuli orangutan (Pongo tapanuliensis), a third species, is classified as critically endangered, with fewer than 800 believed to survive in the wild.
In November, conservationists found the Tapanuli population had been reduced by 7% after severe flooding in Indonesia.
Between 33 and 54 Tapanuli orangutans were estimated to have been killed in widespread floods and landslides in North Sumatra province.
Previous research has suggested annual losses of 1% of the Tapanuli orangutan population would be sufficient to lead to eventual extinction.
The entire Tapanuli population dwells solely in the West Block of the Batang Toru, a forest threatened by mining, palm oil plantations and a large hydropower project.

Info Edge Ventures backed NBFC Ascend Capital’s profitability improved significantly in the fiscal year FY26, growing 6.25X to ₹10 Cr from ₹1.6 Cr in FY25. As per ratings assigned by ICRA, the Jaipur-based EV-focused lender’s total income for the fiscal jumped about 131% to ₹50.3 Cr in FY26 from ₹21.8 Cr in FY25. Its total managed assets (AUM) also expanded 46% to ₹238.6 Cr from ₹163.7 Cr during the period. ICRA noted that the cumulative collection efficiency from Ascend’s securitised EV loan portfolio, comprising of three-wheeler EVs like e-autos, loaders and L5 vehicles, stood at 97.5% as on July 2026, while the 90+ days past due (dpd) delinquency stood at 1.3%. Its gross non-performing assets (GNPA) increased to 2.6% in FY26 from 1.7% in FY25 while capital-to-risk weighted assets ratio (CRAR moderated to 34.8% from 41% a year earlier, though it remained well above the regulatory capital requirement. Despite the healthy pool performance, ICRA highlighted that the NBFC poses risks such as limited operational history and geographical concentration. As of September 2025, Ascend Capital was present across 60 cities in five states and UTs, although its top three states made up for 87.5% of the portfolio. Its total borrower base stood at 18,975 at the time. Tapping The Growing EV Demand Founded in 2019 by Lokesh Chandra and Gaurav Maheshwari, Ascend Capital extends loans of up to ₹2-4 Lakh to consumers looking to buy EVs and batteries for e-rickshaw and L5 vehicles. Ascend originates EV loans through its NBFC and funds its lending book through a mix of institutional debt and securitisation, where pools of EV loans are packaged into securities and sold to investors, allowing the lender to recycle capital into fresh loans. To overcome underwriting and collection challenges related to EV financing, the NBFC has developed an internal benchmark for valuing batteries and maintains a data repository covering OEMs, distributors and drivers. It started disbursing loans against e-autos and e-loaders in January 2024. The NBFC’s PAT stood at just ₹0.1 Cr in FY24, while income stood at ₹13.7 Cr, highlighting a notable acceleration in its scale over the past two years. It also raised ₹50 Cr in equity funding from Info Edge Ventures and Asha Ventures in 2024. The investors own a 24.8% stake in the NBFC as of now. The development comes as a growing set of specialised lenders targets the financing gap in India’s EV ecosystem. A record 24.5 Lakh EVs were sold in India in FY26, up 25% YoY, with electric three-wheelers accounting for 8.31 Lakh units, or 34% of total EV sales, as per Vahan data. E3Ws also crossed a 60% share of India’s overall three-wheeler sales during the year.

'Notices do not mean name deletion': EC clarifies after Kejriwal, Jaishankar, Advani get SIR letters
The clarification came after notices were issued to several prominent political figures during the ongoing SIR in the national capital.
The Election Commission (EC) on Sunday said that notices issued to some voters during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls should not be interpreted as an indication that their names will be removed from the voter list.
The clarification came after several prominent political figures were issued notices during the ongoing SIR of electoral rolls in Delhi. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and her predecessor Arvind Kejriwal were among the 3.31 million electors who received notices over discrepancies in their details, according to election officials. The CEO’s office later clarified that Gupta’s name had been validated after verification.
Also read | LK Advani, Manish Sisodia, Kailash Gahlot among Delhi voters served SIR notices
Deep Dive
BJP veteran LK Advani, former Delhi deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia and BJP MLA Kailash Gahlot were also among those issued notices over “discrepancies” identified during the SIR, officials said.
Other prominent names on the list include External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, former vice-president Jagdeep Dhankhar and Election Commissioner SS Sandhu. They were issued notices over discrepancies in the details furnished during the electoral roll revision exercise.
The CEO office, however, stressed that no elector's name can be deleted without providing an opportunity to be heard and issuing a proper, speaking and appealable order.
Also read | Congress calls SIR ‘Shah Instigated Removal’, flags ‘unusually high’ voter deletions
"All stakeholders are hereby informed that the issue of Notice does not mean that their names will be deleted from the electoral rolls of NCT of Delhi," the CEO office said, adding that system-generated notices are being issued to correct data in ECINET.
"No name can be deleted without giving an opportunity of being heard and a proper speaking and appealable order," it said.
The office also said there was "no existential crisis" arising from the notices, as reported in social and print media.
Why notices are being issued during Delhi SIR
The draft electoral roll was prepared using details submitted by electors through Enumeration Forms to Booth Level Officers (BLOs). It was published on August 31 and is available on the CEO Delhi website, at Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) offices, and at designated polling station locations.
The Election Commission of India announced the SIR in Delhi on May 14 with the objective of ensuring that "No eligible citizen is left out while no ineligible person is included in the Electoral Roll."
As part of the exercise, electors listed in the draft roll have been divided into categories based on whether they or their progeny entries could be mapped or linked with electoral rolls from the last intensive revision.
Notices are being sent to electors whose entries could not be linked with the electoral roll of the last intensive revision, as well as those where "logical discrepancies" were found in the linking process.
Electors can submit documents in response
Those who receive notices can submit their replies and required documents to the concerned ERO or BLO. The CEO office said the list of documents prescribed by the ECI is "only indicative, not exhaustive".
EROs, as statutory authorities, will take decisions on individual cases after considering the documents available and the report submitted by the BLO.
The process of disposing of the notices is scheduled to be completed by October 29. The names of such electors will then be included in the final electoral roll, which is scheduled to be published on November 4.

15 సెప్టెంబర్ 2026న ఉత్తర అరేబియా సముద్రంలో భారత్, పాకిస్తాన్ నావికాదళాలకు చెందిన యుద్ధనౌకలు ఒకదానికొకటి ఢీకొన్నాయి. తమ నౌక సాధారణ నిఘా విధుల్లో ఉండగా పాకిస్తాన్ నౌక వేగంగా, ప్రమాదకరంగా దూసుకొచ్చిందని భారత్ పేర్కొంది. దీనిపై నిరసన తెలుపుతూ సెప్టెంబర్ 16న పాకిస్తాన్ దౌత్యాధికారికి భారత్ సమన్లు జారీ చేసింది. అయితే, పాకిస్తాన్ మాత్రం ఇందుకు భిన్నమైన వాదన వినిపించింది. తమ ‘SEASPARK-26’ నావికా విన్యాసాల్లో ఈ ఘటన జరిగిందని, భారత నౌక ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా తమ నౌక సమీపంలోకి వచ్చిందని ఆరోపించింది.

ఫాక్ట్: ఈ వీడియో 15 సెప్టెంబర్ 2026న భారత్, పాకిస్తాన్ యుద్ధనౌకలు ఢీకొన్న ఘటనకు సంబంధించినది కాదు. వాణిజ్య నౌక ‘ఎంవీ సూయజ్’కు భద్రతగా వెళ్తున్న సమయంలో 2011లో పాకిస్థాన్ నౌక పీఎన్ఎస్ బాబర్, భారత నౌక ఐఎన్ఎస్ గోదావరిని ఢీకొన్న పాత సంఘటనకు సంబంధించిన వీడియో ఇది. కావున, పోస్టులో చేయబడిన క్లెయిమ్ తప్పుదోవ పట్టించే విధంగా ఉంది.
ముందుగా వైరల్ వీడియోలోని దృశ్యాలను రివర్స్ ఇమేజ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, ఇదే వీడియోని 16 అక్టోబర్ 2014న “mix” అనే యూట్యూబ్ ఛానెల్లో అప్లోడ్ (ఆర్కైవ్) చేసినట్లు గుర్తించాం. ఈ వీడియోలో పాకిస్తాన్ నౌక బాబర్ భారత నౌకతో పోటీ పడుతుందని పేర్కొనబడింది. ఏడెన్ అఖాతంలో (Gulf of Aden) ‘ఎంవీ సూయజ్’ అనే వాణిజ్య నౌకను రక్షించే సమయంలో తీసిన భారత, పాకిస్తాన్ నౌకల దృశ్యాలను ఈ వీడియో చూపుతుందని వివరణలో రాసి ఉంది. దీన్ని బట్టి, వైరల్ వీడియో సెప్టెంబర్ 2026 నాటి ఘటనకు సంబంధించినది కాదని, అది దశాబ్దానికి పైగా పాతదని స్పష్టమవుతుంది.
దీనికి సంబంధించిన మరింత సమాచారం కోసం ఇంటర్నెట్లో వెతకగా, ఇదే ఘటన గురించి చెప్తున్నా 2011 నాటి NDTV వార్తా కథనం లభించింది. ఈ కథనం ప్రకారం, ఈ ఘటన 16 జూన్ 2011న జరిగింది. వాణిజ్య నౌక ‘ఎంవీ సూయజ్’కు భద్రతగా వెళ్తున్న సమయంలో, భారత నావికాదళానికి చెందిన ‘ఐఎన్ఎస్ గోదావరి’ నౌకను దాటి వెళ్లే ప్రయత్నంలో పాకిస్తాన్ యుద్ధనౌక ‘పీఎన్ఎస్ బాబర్’ దాని వెనుక భాగాన్ని ఢీకొట్టింది. సముద్రం అల్లకల్లోలంగా ఉన్న సమయంలో ఐఎన్ఎస్ గోదావరికి అతి సమీపంలోకి వచ్చిన పీఎన్ఎస్ బాబర్ రాసుకుంటూ వెళ్లిందని, దీనివల్ల భారత నౌకలోని హెలికాప్టర్ డెక్కు నష్టం వాటిల్లిందని ఆ కథనం పేర్కొంది. నౌకలు ఢీకొన్న తర్వాత పాకిస్తాన్ నౌక సిబ్బంది సంబరాలు చేసుకుంటున్న దృశ్యాలను కూడా ఆ కథనం చూపించింది.
18 జూన్ 2011న భారత విదేశీ వ్యవహారాల మంత్రిత్వ శాఖ ఒక పత్రికా ప్రకటన విడుదల చేసి పాకిస్తాన్ తీరుపై నిరసన వ్యక్తం చేసింది. పీఎన్ఎస్ బాబర్ చేసిన ప్రమాదకరమైన విన్యాసాలు ఐఎన్ఎస్ గోదావరి నౌక, దాని సిబ్బంది భద్రతను ప్రమాదంలో పడేశాయని అందులో పేర్కొంది. అంతేకాకుండా, పాకిస్తాన్ చర్యలు అంతర్జాతీయ సముద్ర భద్రతా నిబంధనలను, అలాగే సైనిక విన్యాసాలకు ముందస్తు సమాచారం ఇవ్వాలనే 1991 నాటి ఇండో-పాక్ ఒప్పందాన్ని ఉల్లంఘించాయని భారత్ స్పష్టం చేసింది.

Mahanadi water dispute likely to be resolved soon: Chhattisgarh CM
The dispute over sharing of Mahanadi waters has continued for more than a decade, with Odisha objecting to the construction of barrages by Chhattisgarh
The long-standing Mahanadi water-sharing dispute between Chhattisgarh and Odisha is likely to be resolved soon through discussions and technical consultations between the two states, Chhattisgarh chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai said on Monday.
Speaking to reporters at Swami Vivekananda Airport after returning from a two-day visit to Odisha, Sai said he discussed the issue with Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi and stressed that there was no scope for conflict between the two states over the river water.
“The Mahanadi water issue is going to be resolved very soon. Both states have BJP [Bharatiya Janata Party] governments and there is an NDA government at the Centre. There is no situation of dispute anywhere,” Sai said.
He said the matter, which was earlier being heard by the Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal, has now been referred to the Central Water Commission (CWC).
The dispute over sharing of Mahanadi waters has continued for more than a decade, with Odisha objecting to the construction of barrages by Chhattisgarh in the upstream areas. Odisha has maintained that these structures affect the flow of water into the downstream areas, particularly during the lean season.
Odisha approached the Union water resources ministry in 2016, raising objections to the construction of six barrages in Chhattisgarh for industrial purposes and alleging reduced downstream flow during the non-monsoon period.
Following a suit filed by Odisha in the Supreme Court, the Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted in 2018 to adjudicate the dispute.
The issue gained renewed attention in recent months, with both states signalling their willingness to find an amicable solution through dialogue and technical consultations.
On July 30, the Centre facilitated a meeting between Sai and Majhi, chaired by Union Jal Shakti minister CR Patil, as part of efforts to find a mutually acceptable solution to the dispute.
The Mahanadi is considered the lifeline of Chhattisgarh, with around 78% of the state’s population living in its basin. The state is also part of the basins of five major rivers — Mahanadi, Godavari, Ganga, Brahmani and Narmada.

Former husband, in-laws of Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi stand trial in her killing
A murder trial has begun for the former husband and in-laws of Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi
HONG KONG -- A murder trial began Monday for the former husband and in-laws of Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi more than three years after the discovery of parts of her dismembered body at a house shocked the city where violent crime is rare.
Choi's ex-husband Alex Kwong, his father Kwong Kau and his brother Anthony Kwong were accused of killing Choi in February 2023. They face life imprisonment if convicted of murder. They were also charged with preventing the lawful burial of a body.
Choi was a 28-year-old socialite who shared her glamorous life of photo shoots and fashion shows on Instagram. Days before her death, she posted about attending a Dior show at Paris Fashion Week.
Choi's killing transfixed many in the Asian financial hub that has a very low level of violent crime. Dozens of people waited outside the courtroom for the hearing to start, and a live broadcast was arranged for people to watch outside it.
All three defendants wore masks and appeared calm in court. Kwong Kau was in a white T-shirt, while his sons wore suits.
Police in 2023 said they found some body parts inside the unit at a village in Tai Po, a suburban district in Hong Kong. Officers later searched a landfill for evidence.
Choi had two children with Alex Kwong. She remarried after their divorce and had two younger children with her second husband.
The prosecution is expected to open its case at a later date. The jury trial is expected to last 45 days.

Texas mom arrested for giving away her baby to a stranger at a bus stop, cops say
The teen mom left her newborn with the stranger in San Antonio and fled in an Uber
An 18-year-old Texas mom has been arrested after giving away her one-month-old baby to a stranger she met at a bus stop, police said.
Karla Ibarra was carrying her infant at a bus stop in downtown San Antonio September 13 when she approached Jennifer Benavides and asked to use her cellphone, KSAT reported.
Benavides was fawning over Ibarra’s baby when the teen handed him over — along with all his federal ID documents — and asked if she wanted to take him.
“She’s like, ‘Well, do you want him? I’m going to give him away. I’m going to give him to somebody,” Benavides recalled.
“She begins handing me his birth certificate, his Medicaid, his Social Security card,” she said.
Realizing Ibarra was being serious about giving her baby away, Benavides brought her to the home of a friend who lived nearby — but the teen mom quickly left the house in an Uber without her son.
Benavides called 911 and she and her friend cared for the baby while they waited for police to arrive.
Ibarra later returned to the home, where she was arrested. The teen mom is charged with abandoning and endangering a child with intent to return.
“It’s upsetting to know that, with even all the resources that we have out there, that somebody would just do this,” Benavides said.
Following Ibarra’s arrest, her child was placed with other relatives, Child Protective Services confirmed.
Texas has the Baby Moses Law, which allows a parent to legally and anonymously surrender their newborn at designated locations without facing any criminal penalties.
The infant must be 60 days old or younger to be left at locations, which include fire stations and hospitals. The baby must be physically handed to an employee or placed in a Safe Baby Box.
The Independent has contacted the San Antonio Police Department for more information.
A judge set Ibarra’s bail at $7,000.

An Islamic State group member was sentenced on Wednesday to 20 years in prison for aiding the terrorist organization that took credit for a suicide bombing that killed 13 US service members and about 160 Afghans at the Kabul airport five years ago during the US military’s chaotic withdrawal from the country.
A federal jury in Virginia had convicted Mohammad Sharifullah in April of providing material support to the IS affiliate known as Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP). But jurors could not agree whether he bore some responsibility for the airport bombing on 26 August 2021.
US troops were conducting an evacuation operation at the airport when a suicide bomber detonated an improvised explosive device near an entry point known as Abbey Gate. Sharifullah’s role in the attack was scouting a route to Hamid Karzai international airport, prosecutors said.
Sharifullah, 28, received the maximum sentence for his one-count conviction in an international terrorism case that Donald Trump heralded last year during a speech to a joint session of Congress.
Sharifullah did not testify at his trial and declined to address the court before the US district judge Anthony Trenga imposed the sentence. The judge said the defendant was a “dedicated terrorist” who expressed no remorse for the “unfathomable” grief and suffering that he had caused.
Trenga heard victim impact statements from several parents of US service members. From a podium only a few feet from where Sharifullah sat, they took turns paying tribute to their children’s sacrifices and describing how the attack has shattered their families.
Mark Schmitz of Missouri asked Sharifullah to turn and look at him as he spoke about the life and death of his 20-year-old son, Marine Corps L/Cpl Jared Schmitz.
“They may have taken his life, but they’ll never take his legacy,” Mark Schmitz said. “A bomb killed my son. It did not kill what he stood for.”
Paula Knauss-Selph, whose son, army SSgt Ryan Knauss, was killed in the Abbey Gate bombing, said the family was “forever changed” by the attack.
“No justice will ever be enough to mend my broken heart,” she said.
Sharifullah requested a 17-year prison sentence, while prosecutors sought 20 years. His lawyers said he was never an ISKP leader and had not been convicted of any conduct related to the airport suicide bombing.
“He was brought here because the government believed he participated in the Abbey Gate attack, a theory which it was unable to prove at trial,” defense attorneys wrote.
Prosecutors said in their sentencing memo that “from his teenage years, when he pledged an oath of allegiance to [ISKP], Sharifullah’s carnage was driven by hate. Hate towards Americans.”
Jurors convicted Sharifullah of providing material support to ISKP. They deadlocked on whether any deaths at the airport “resulted from” that conspiracy. Sharifullah could have faced a possible life sentence if the jury had unanimously decided that question.
According to prosecutors, Sharifullah told a journalist that he wanted to “catch and kill the crusaders” from the United States for invading his country after the attacks of September 11. They said Sharifullah was involved in dozens of other attacks, including a March 2024 assault on a Moscow concert hall that killed roughly 140 people.
Defense lawyers argued that prosecutors failed to present any evidence tying Sharifullah to the Kabul bombing besides his own words during hours of FBI questioning. His team said Sharifullah told FBI agents what he thought they wanted to hear, possibly because he was afraid of being tortured in Pakistani custody before he was brought to the US.
A review by US Central Command found that the Abbey Gate bomber was Abdul Rahman al-Logari, an IS member who had been released from an Afghan prison by the Taliban. According to an FBI affidavit, Sharifullah recognized the alleged bomber as an operative he had known while incarcerated.

One mobile number, two phones: What is iPhone handoff and which carriers support it?
If you switch between two iPhones regularly, you're going to love this new feature.
If you use two iPhones, you no longer need to run separate carrier accounts for each of them, thanks to a new iOS 27 feature: iPhone Handoff.
Mentioned briefly at WWDC and in more detail during Apple's Surprise and Shine event on September 9, iPhone Handoff lets you use the same phone number across two iPhones; in typical Apple fashion, the feature is so easy it's almost invisible. Once you set it up, all you have to do is unlock the iPhone you want to use, and you're ready to go.
Handoff lets you take and make calls and messages on both phones using the same number, add payment cards on one device to work on both, and interact seamlessly with most apps and iCloud. There are some limitations; for example, your carrier must support iPhone Handoff, it does not switch your paired Apple Watch between devices, and some wallet items like IDs and passes won't work, but most features work seamlessly. In this article, you'll learn how to set up iPhone Handoff, how to use it and which carriers support it.
Setting up iPhone Handoff
You can set iPhone Handoff up on any two devices running iOS 27 or later. Both must be on the same Wi-Fi network and signed into the same Apple Account for iCloud, FaceTime and iMessage. One phone will be the primary phone, and one will be your secondary phone. The primary device holds the main eSIM and manages carrier settings, but you can also use each phone's eSIM, so long as both are from supporting carriers.
While we expect that more will do so, only T-Mobile in the US and Telekom in Germany have confirmed support so far, with T-Mobile charging an additional $5 monthly fee. Here's how to set it up on your iPhones.
- Place your two iPhones next to each other and unlock one.
- Navigate to Settings > Cellular, and tap Set Up Cellular/Add eSIM, or iPhone Handoff if a number is already set up on the device.
- Choose Use Number on This iPhone and Another, tap Continue and follow the on-screen prompts to assign one device as your main iPhone.
It is worth noting that once it's time to replace one iPhone with another, you must transfer the eSIM to the new device. If you want to disable Handoff completely, Apple says you'll need to contact your carrier.
Why and how to use iPhone Handoff
Apple has designed iPhone Handoff to be as easy to use as picking up your iPhone and unlocking it, which is literally all you need to do. A small notification will appear in your Dynamic Island just under the Wi-Fi indicator to let you know your device is activated for iPhone Handoff.
While it's nice to have, iPhone Handoff is also a niche feature. However, you might find it useful as you migrate between an old and new iPhone, to easily carry an older and less valuable device when you travel, or to use a more portable or cheaper iPhone alongside a $2,000 iPhone Duo. Professionals using different devices for work and personal life may also find use for the feature.

73 goals from dropping deep - we ask Kane to break down how he did it
- Published
As Harry Kane's career has progressed, the 33-year-old has taken an increasingly complete role, popping up to collect the ball as deep as his own box.
Many wonder why a talisman tasked with scoring doesn't spend more time closer to goal, but last season the England and Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals - the highest tally of his career - while playing deeper than he ever has done.
When I mention this paradox, a grin spreads across his face.
"Until you really understand football and understand what we've been talking about, it's so easy to say 'stay high, you're going to score' but it doesn't work like that," Kane says.
I sat down to speak to Kane about the finer details of his game, shedding light on his unique role.
Watching Kane train, his professionalism is palpable. England's record goalscorer is one of the first out on the pitch. The younger players indulge in playful kick-ups as he watches, engaged in conversation with a member of staff.
From a distance, that makes it easy to confuse him with a coach but, given his role on the pitch, it is a fitting mistake.
Kane's style of play reflects who he is as a person, with those who know him saying he is well-rounded and humble on and off the pitch.
The season is in its infancy but Kane isn't basking in the success of the past 12 months. With only five days of pre-season training under his belt, the England captain completed 90 minutes of Bayern's 2-1 win over Borussia Dortmund to lift the German Super Cup.
As demanding as his roaming role is, he has taken the physical demands of it in his stride. Across the past six seasons, STATSports - a sports technology company Kane has invested in - found his distance covered, high-speed running and accelerations were up 8%, 22% and 42% respectively.
And given how the tactical landscape has changed over that time, it is particularly impressive Kane has been able to not only keep up, but stay ahead.
"Over the last five or six years, man-to-man pressure has become bigger," Kane says.
"European football is physical and top teams are trying to win the ball back high, trusting their defenders and midfielders to defend man for man to win their battles."
Given that change, the best teams have recruited physical athletes and brilliant dribblers who can beat their man when the game becomes a series of one-against-ones.
Kane, not known for his dribbling - and by his own admission "not the fastest", has thrived on his own terms.
Against Dortmund, there was a specific moment Kane dropped deep, looking to arrive in space unmarked. Recognising the danger, two players converged on the Englishman.
Kane's dribbling is cerebral. His speed of thought provides him solutions to problems others would attempt to solve with their feet alone.
After getting low and using his strength to shrug centre-back Waldemar Anton off him, Kane rose, slightly adjusting his body to the right. These micro-adjustments are a hallmark of his game and through them he is able to shift an entire team's momentum.
Fooled by this feint, Daniel Svensson and Jobe Bellingham found themselves wrong-footed as Kane snapped the ball back the other way, opening up the entire pitch from within Bayern's half.
1 of 4
Earlier this year, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany shed light on Kane's unique role, explaining it as being 50% coached and 50% Kane deciding what to do.
"I think it's partly instinct, using my football brain and getting the feeling on the pitch," says Kane. "If, for example, I want to drop and see if the centre-back really wants to commit, he might commit into midfield, but is he going to commit if I drop all the way to my box?
"After the first five or 10 minutes you really get an understanding of how the opposition are going to play, which dictates how I play."
There is a shared understanding at Bayern of an approach that allows team-mates to make sense of rotations that, to the naked eye, appear random.
Kane, who is given more freedom than most, is at the centre of it.
"I feel like my position now is as one of two 10s, and you work together," he says. "You can double up on one side to overload, which causes the opposition centre-backs a problem of who to mark.
"If they want to mark both, they've got to go man-to-man and then that leaves space for our wingers or full-backs to run into.
"It's posing all these questions to the opposition but, personally, I love having someone close to me who I can link with."
Kane built his reputation playing as a lone number nine, so it is interesting to hear him identify instead as a number 10 - in a front two.
"When you're the number nine on your own you can get marked by two centre-backs and you struggle to get touches on the ball," he says. "You're relying on everyone else to find you with the ball."
Showing Kane two clips from last season, I ask him to talk through what was going through his head.
"The thing with our formation is, as long as there's someone in each position, it doesn't really matter who it is. Lucho [Luis Diaz] in this clip is playing as one of those 10s.
"I've come off to try and create a bit of space and Lucho's gone through the centre."
Distracted by Kane's dropping-deep movement, one of the opposition midfielders is pulled towards him. This creates space, allowing Joshua Kimmich to punch the ball through to Diaz.
"I think it's Serge [Gnabry] making the run in behind which takes the defenders back, which allows me and Lucho that space in between. Lucho lays it off and whenever I'm in that position, around 20-25 yards out, I'm always looking if I can get my shot off."
It is one of many examples of Kane initially dropping deep before scoring.
"By playing deep when the play develops, I end up coming into a number 10 spot when everyone's dropped," he says. "I can get shots off from the edge of the box, which is a big strength of mine, or I'm running off the back of players where no-one's picking me up - because the midfielder finds it hard to [track]."
1 of 3
The second clip is from Bayern's Champions League tie against Club Brugge.
Usually Kane is marked by an opposition centre-back, but the Belgian club give that responsibility to their holding midfielder - something he recognises and exploits.
Lennart Karl scores without Kane touching the ball, but the striker's involvement is undeniable.
"These are the little runs, again, not everyone sees," Kane explains. "With Jamal Musiala and Lenny, they're so good at receiving the ball and dribbling so there'll be times where I will actually stay higher and let those guys get on the ball a bit deeper, and I'll try and make runs in behind.
"Without changing my game too much, I try and complement the players around me.
"I know Lenny is so good in those pockets and when he gets there, I'm more thinking of running in behind because, one, he can play me in and I can go through on goal, or two, he can dribble with the ball and do exactly what happened here.
"As soon as Lenny gets in that pocket I make the run and not always to get the ball, sometimes it is just to drag the defender away.
"Now he's one-against-one with a centre-back in the middle of the pitch and that's dangerous for any centre-back."
1 of 3
With the Ballon d'Or announcement on the horizon, Kane's name is in the conversation, primarily for the sheer volume of goals he has scored. What is easier to miss in that debate is the rest of his game.
Kane plays for the team in each phase of the game across the entirety of the pitch, while at the same time producing extraordinary individual numbers that match the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland.
He has described himself as playing in the role of a number 10, nine and six at times.
In a football world of specific and heavily drilled tactical roles, that is quite the achievement.

Srinagar, Sep 21: J&K Peoples Conference President and MLA Handwara Sajad Lone launched a scathing attack on the National Conference government on Monday after assembly data revealed a devastating gap between election promises and ground reality on the recruitment front.
Speaking after the assembly adjournment, he raised a pointed question on recruitment figures. Lone said the data had exposed ugly truths about the false promises made by the NC government.
"The NC manifesto is a litany of lies," he declared making clear he was not speaking in abstractions but backing every word with cold hard numbers extracted from the government's own records.
On the most glaring failure Lone pointed out that the NC manifesto had promised one lakh new jobs to the people of Jammu and Kashmir. Against that promise the government has managed to create only 899 jobs till date. Doing the math Lone delivered a damning verdict.
"At the current rate it will take them 222.46 years to create one lakh jobs. What a joke." He paused before adding what he called the more painful truth. "The bigger joke is on those people who bought this lie."
The second broken promise relates to vacancies in government departments.
The NC had committed in its manifesto to fill all vacant posts within 180 days of coming to power. The assembly data tells a starkly different story with only 7580 vacancies filled in the past two years while 40672 posts continue to remain vacant. Breaking down the numbers Lone noted that 24427 non-gazetted posts remain unfilled alongside 3318 gazetted posts and 12927 multi-tasking staff positions still lying empty.
"At this pace it will take more than a decade to fill up these 40672 posts," he said leaving the treasury benches with little room to respond.
The third broken promise involves application fees for government jobs. NC had publicly committed to waiving off these fees so that financial burden would not become a barrier for job aspirants. Lone revealed that he had submitted a question on this very issue in the assembly a year ago and the answer that came back was deeply damning.
"It turned out the same government had collected crores in application fees," he said highlighting the brazen contradiction between promise and practice.(KNS)

Vivo’s new X500 flagship phones have arrived in China, and as usual the company’s focus is firmly on photography. The X500 Pro Max — a new tier in its lineup — is the first phone to use new sensors and silicon from Sony and MediaTek that enable impressive dynamic range and slow-motion video recording.
Vivo’s X500 Pro Max has 17 stops of dynamic range and 4K240 slo-mo
The X500, X500 Pro, and X500 Pro Max launch this month in China, with a global release on the way later.
The X500 Pro Max uses Sony’s new Lytia L910 image sensor, its first to use LOFIC, a sensor technology that enables expanded dynamic range. The 50-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch-type sensor delivers what Vivo calls “true 17 EV ultra-high dynamic range,” more than the 16.5 stops claimed by the Xiaomi 17 Ultra. The excellent 200-megapixel, 3.7x telephoto from the X300 Ultra returns here too, along with support for that phone’s 400mm teleconverter lens.
The X500 Pro and Pro Max are also the first phones run on MediaTek’s new Dimensity 9600 Pro, with the 9600M found in the base X500. The 2nm Pro chip brings with it the usual performance bumps, but also the ability to record 4K 240fps slow-motion video. 10bit Log recording and new cinematic video styles are included too.

Today’s launch is China-only, but a global launch is coming, though we don’t yet know when.

EAM Jaishankar to lead Indian delegation at UN General Assembly
Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will address the general debate on September 24, followed by Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif the next day
External affairs minister S Jaishankar will lead the Indian delegation attending the United Nations General Assembly this week, the external affairs ministry said on Sunday.
Jaishankar’s address at the high level session of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York is scheduled for September 26, the ministry said. During the visit, Jaishankar will also attend different plurilateral and bilateral meetings.
The general debate during September 22-28 is the annual meeting of heads of state and government at the beginning of the General Assembly session, featuring world leaders making statements outlining their country’s position. Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman will preside over the General Assembly session, the theme for which is “Restoring trust, managing transformation: A UN that delivers for all”.
Also Read:West Asia war to resume? Iran warns of fresh US action amid deadlock over peace deal
Prime Minister Narendra Modi skipped the UN General Assembly last year too, and the Indian delegation was led by Jaishankar.
Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will address the general debate on September 24, followed by Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif the next day.
This year’s General Assembly session aims at revitalising global cooperation, giving a critical push to the Sustainable Development Goals, and driving collective action for peace, dignity and equality on a healthy planet.
Meetings scheduled during the General Assembly session include a high-level gathering to commemorate the 40th anniversary of the Declaration on the Right to Development, a meeting on climate action and just transition, and a high-level meeting on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response.

There will also be a high-level meeting to address existential threats posed by sea level rise, and a plenary meeting to commemorate the International Day for the Total Elimination of Nuclear Weapons.
This will be the last General Assembly session for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, whose second five-year tenure ends in December.

An 11-year-old boy has been taken to hospital in a serious condition after being shot in a home in Sydney’s north-west.
The child was receiving life-saving treatment in hospital on Monday night after suffering gunshot wounds to his face and neck, police said.
He was found injured at about 5pm at a unit on Fairway Drive, Norwest, after emergency services arrived in response to reports of a shooting at the property.
Paramedics treated the boy at the scene before taking him to hospital.
Initial reports indicated the shots were fired from within the home.
Speaking a few hours after the incident, Supt Naomi Moore said four 18-year-old men and a 44-year-old woman had been inside the unit at the time, all of whom were unharmed and were assisting with the investigation.
Three of the 18-year-olds had been arrested, Moore said.
Moore said while the investigation was just starting, police had no information to suggest the incident was related to organised crime.
There have been at least six suspected mistaken-identity shootings in Sydney since the start of last year.
Last week, two teenage boys were charged with murder after the recent shooting death of a university student in Sydney, which police say was a case of mistaken identity.
Moore assured people in the community who were “fearful on the streets at the moment” that police did not believe Monday’s shooting in Norwood was related to organised crime.
Police were investigating how the gun came to be in the house, as there were no firearms registered to that address, she said.
Moore said she was not sure what type of gun had been used, or where the weapon was located.
“In terms of what happened in that apartment, it is far too early for me to say right now,” she said.
“[But] we have all sorts of resources down there … to ensure that we do get to the bottom of what happened in that unit tonight.”
Police had established an “expansive” crime scene as investigations into the incident continued.
“It’s a tragic situation with an 11-year-old child suffering this injury,” Moore said.
“The mother is with the child at the moment – she is as distressed as any parent would be about what she is dealing with at the moment.”

- Psyonix revealed a new look at Rocket League in Unreal Engine 6 in a mini-docu-style clip.

It’s no secret that Psyonix has been building a new version of Rocket League, and it will officially be the first game to run on Unreal Engine 6. Now, developers have offered a first look at the gameplay of Rocket League in UE6 in a new behind-the-scenes clip where Psyonix can be seen taking real-time feedback from RLCS (Rocket League Championship Series) pros.
New Rocket League Gameplay Clip Shows Pros Playtesting Unreal Engine 6 Build
In the clip shared on the Rocket League X page, Psyonix revealed they hosted several playtest sessions in June and August this year in Cary and Paris, with Rocket League pros. These included RLCS athletes like JSTN, Firstkiller, Archie, and more.
Players like Archie said that in the new UE6 version of Rocket League there were some mechanics “that felt a bit off and laggy and hard to do”, to which RLCS pro Zen followed by saying (translated from French), “The developers, they listened to us a lot. They took our feedback really seriously.”

His Hyundai Santa Fe burst into flames on busy highway after repairs at dealership
168 Hyundai vehicle fires were reported to Transport Canada over the past decade
Three months after a "traumatizing" vehicle fire, Jason Pelletier is still waiting for answers — and hoping for more compensation — from automaker Hyundai.
On June 9, during the morning commute to work, the school principal was driving on a busy highway, just north of Toronto, when his Santa Fe suddenly caught fire. He saw thick black smoke and flames billowing from the hood. He says the engine and brakes were no longer responsive.
"I'm trying to cross five lanes of traffic on the 401 in morning traffic," Pelletier said. He says he initially struggled to open the door, but finally made it out of the vehicle.
"I got out and, 20 seconds later, there was an explosion," he said. "The whole front end blew up."
What Pelletier finds even more unsettling is that he had just taken his SUV to the dealership the day before. He had to replace a head gasket, a critical seal located between an engine's block and cylinder head that maintains combustion pressure and prevents coolant and oil from mixing.
He says he noticed a burning smell shortly after leaving the downtown Toronto dealership, but wasn’t too worried because the service manager said it might be from residue after the service.
He later sent text messages to the service manager, asking whether he should be concerned about the light smoke coming out from the hood.
The next morning, on his way to work, a message popped up on his vehicle’s touchscreen, warning of a "potential condition" with the engine control system and recommending a "full system check."
Pelletier sent a few more text messages — but the service manager did not reply before the engine burst into flames.
"They reached out and made sure I was alive essentially," he said.
Safety is 'top priority'
Hyundai Canada declined our request for an interview, but told CBC News in an emailed statement that safety is its "top priority."
"The circumstances surrounding this matter are still under review and we cannot comment further at this time," said Nitish Bissonauth, senior manager of corporate communications.
Joe Hakim, general manager of the dealership, stated in an email to Pelletier that Hycay Consulting Engineering had been commissioned to conduct a joint investigation with the insurance company to determine the cause of the fire.
Hyundai Canada did not respond to questions regarding other vehicle fires reported to the company or the preventive measures put in place in recent years.
Over the past decade — from Jan. 1, 2016 to Sept. 8, 2026 — Transport Canada received 1,140 reports of vehicle fires, across all makes and models. But it says there is no obligation to report these incidents to the ministry, so this number could be higher.
"Fires are about one in 2,500 cars in Canada," according to Murray Thomson, a combustion specialist and professor of mechanical engineering at the University of Toronto
"If you add it up across all of Canada, you have 10,000 vehicle fires per year. That is significant."
With 168 of the 1,140 reported fires, Hyundai accounted for roughly 15 per cent of incidents during this period. The Korean automaker ranks second, behind Ford. The ministry did not provide year-by-year data for each automaker.
A joint investigation by CBC Marketplace and Go Public, published in 2021, focused on seven cases involving Hyundai and Kia vehicles when engines had stalled or caught fire.
"If a car has recurring issues, that's obviously a concern," Murray said.
In 2023, Hyundai recalled more than 320,000 vehicles in Canada linked to a potential fault in the anti-lock braking system that could cause a fire. Pelletier’s Santa Fe was not affected by that recall but it was impacted by two others.
It was fitted with a Knock Sensor Detection System, which warns the driver if their engine is about to fail, in 2020 and, three years later, was fixed again because of a fire risk "even when the vehicle is stationary and the engine is switched off," as Hyundai warned in its safety recall.
Thomson says automakers remain responsible for the safe operation throughout a vehicle’s lifetime, but admits that it can be difficult when cars change hands. "There could be a system to track ownership more clearly, to link the current owner to the manufacturer directly," he said.
"That's what the whole recall system is about. Transport Canada plays a role too, because it tracks, collects information, and sometimes requests recalls or identifies issues that the manufacturer should respond to."
Transport Canada has conducted several investigations into parts and components of Hyundai vehicles, many of which have led to safety recalls. The federal ministry is currently investigating the trailer lighting module in 2019 to 2023 Santa Fe models, saying two reported fires may be linked to that part.
"In the majority of vehicle fires, the damage caused is significant, making it difficult to determine the exact origin and cause of the fire," the ministry stated in an email to Radio-Canada, adding that vehicle fires can result from various factors, such as inadequate maintenance, improper repairs or manufacturing defects. Arson is also included in its figures.
"Transport Canada does not have data that would allow it to reliably assign a specific percentage to the various potential causes of vehicle fires."
Lengthy claims process
Pelletier’s insurer paid him nearly $22,000 — the estimated value of the vehicle before the fire — on top of the cost of a rental car for one month.
But according to his own estimates, he has lost more than $5,000 worth of personal belongings, including AirPods, pairs of glasses, sportswear and accessories for his dogs.
That’s not to mention the many drag outfits, accessories and make up products that were in his SUV when it burned. The fire happened during Pride Month, a particularly busy time of year for his alter ego, Jezebel Bardot.
"I’m not trying to become a millionaire out of this. I just don’t want to be worse off than I was when I handed them the keys on Monday June 8th to have my car repaired," he said.
Three months later, the Toronto resident is astounded that his Santa Fe, currently stored in distant Oshawa, is still under forensic investigation. He wonders whether yet another recall could have prevented this ordeal.
"I'm certainly hoping that they're not knowingly gambling with people's lives."
In the meantime, he has decided to buy a new SUV — opting for a different brand. "I don't think you could pay me to drive a Hyundai at this point. And it's too bad from a guy who was a longtime fan."

MS NOW, CNN and Politico to sue Trump administration over White House ban
Trump said Friday he would ban all 3 outlets because of coverage he disliked
MS NOW, CNN and Politico said on Monday they were suing the Trump administration to protect their First Amendment rights after U.S. President Donald Trump's announcement that he would ban the news outlets from the White House's building grounds.
The three news organizations said they had notified the government they were filing their lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia and could see emergency hearings in the case as soon as this week.
"Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting. Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference," they wrote in a joint statement.
The lawsuit aims "to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," they added.
Representatives for the White House did not respond to a request for comment.
Trump defended the ban in another social media post on Monday after the lawsuit was announced, calling the news media a security threat, without providing any evidence.
"The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish. It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS," he wrote. "It is corrupt, purposeful, pervasive, fully coordinated, and totally out of control. It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!"
The Trump administration has upended decades of tradition in dealings between the White House and press, denying the access many major news organizations have had to the president while elevating new media outlets seen as more sympathetic to the administration. He has also filed a number of lawsuits against news organizations.
Trump's latest move comes as his fellow Republicans seek to defend their narrow majorities in Congress in the November midterm elections as polls show the public souring on Republicans and Trump's own approval ratings stand near historic lows.

- Trump announces White House ban on CNN, other media outlets
On Saturday, all three outlets said their journalists were turned away from the White House grounds and their press credentials confiscated, a day after Trump initially announced his ban in a social media post and threatened to block other outlets.
He later addressed what he called his "ban on the free press" with reporters at an event in the Oval Office and said there was no particular incident that provoked the move.
Asked what other news organizations could be targeted, Trump cited the New York Times and the Washington Post as "fake news" but said they had not been removed yet.
The Associated Press, the White House Correspondents' Association and others have criticized Trump's ban, citing the fundamental American right to free speech and calling for access to be immediately restored.
The Associated Press filed its own lawsuit after being barred along with Reuters last year from the group of reporters that cover the president's daily movements.

In a three-day strategic dialogue, Belgium and WHO reviewed progress in their longstanding partnership, and agreed to further boost their collaboration on universal health coverage, health-systems strengthening and equitable access to essential vaccines, medicines and health technologies.
The Belgian delegation – headed by H.E. Christophe Payot, Ambassador of Belgium to the United Nations and other international organizations in Geneva – discussed issues of strategic importance, exchanged views on how to smoothly align WHO strategic directions and Belgium's development cooperation priorities in the context of an evolving global health landscape.
The partners exchanged updates on Belgium's support to global health areas brought in the spotlight during the Belgian presidency of Council of the European Union in 2024. WHO was represented by leadership and technical experts from Headquarters and from the Regional Offices for Africa and for Europe.
"After listening to the leaders and experts of WHO we now better understand how they are navigating these challenging times", said Mr Koen Van Acoleyen, Minister Counselor at the Permanent Representation of Belgium to the UN. "We are honoured that we can walk this road together."
Accelerating equitable access to vaccines, medicines and health technologies
The partners reviewed the current status and the most noticeable results achieved by the Access to Medicines programme funded by Belgium. WHO illustrated its work and challenges with an example of country-level implementation in Senegal. It also explained WHO's policies and work on equitable access and local production. Both parties recognized a shared goal for sustainability of the Access to Medicines initiative, as market shaping is key to ensure long-term success.
Health emergencies and pandemic prevention, preparedness and response
Discussions covered WHO's role in strengthening the global architecture for health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience, including the pandemic agreement negotiations and the One Health approach. WHO's crucial field work on health emergency response was demonstrated by presenting the activities in Gaza. The debate also touched upon threats posed by acceleration of biological risks and zoonoses, along with WHO engagement, in particular, risk mitigation.
Universal Health Coverage (UHC)
Elaborating on progress made on UHC-Partnership, the participants reviewed results achieved by WHO with Belgium support in the period 2021-2024, specifically in Belgium's partner countries. They discussed the way forward, exploring the potential for enhanced collaboration at country level, including eventual alignment between WHO country office programmes and Belgium's country level bilateral cooperation. Examples included a summary of the work and challenges at country level from the Democratic Republic of Congo. The visitors listened to a recap of WHO's policies and work on mental health in the context of primary health care.
The partners also reviewed progress in other areas of collaboration on WHO programmes supported by Belgium, such as Neglected Tropical Diseases and Sexual, Reproductive Health and Rights. The review underpinned the importance of an evidence-based approach in these areas.
WHO appreciates Belgium's commitment and engagement, displayed by the participation of representatives of the country's Federal government as well as the Flemish and Walloon governments. "We thank you for your support, honesty, and strong engagement for global health", said Dr Catharina Boehme, Assistant Director-General, External Relations and Governing Bodies. "Your efforts in supporting our work in Mozambique and Senegal are clear examples of the crucial work we accomplish together".
Looking into the future
The partners discussed ways forward for the Belgium-WHO collaboration framework and multi-year agreement, including progress towards a renewed WHO-Belgium Country Cooperation Strategy.
The enhanced collaboration between Belgium and WHO will support a strong global health agenda under the WHO 14th General Programme of Work (GPW14). There was a shared vision that UHC and health systems strengthening being at the heart of GPW14 ambitions will be taken as essential scope in WHO's ongoing prioritization work.
"We recognize WHO as a trustworthy partner in global health. We felt proud hearing how crucial our support is to the Organization and how it is having a positive impact at country, regional, and global levels", said Mr Dirk Brems, Director of Thematic and Multilateral Cooperation, Directorate-General Development Cooperation and Humanitarian Aid. "It's important we continue these discussions as we tread uncharted territories, and we look forward to working together for strong and sustained multilateralism".

Two men that the Trump administration expelled to Equatorial Guinea were bound, fitted with bags over their heads, beaten and pushed down a flight of stairs, all in plain view of other US deportees, according to witnesses and human rights lawyers.
The men – one from Egypt and one from Eritrea – were then taken to a prison. About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. Detainees have said they believe the men were beaten for telling the press and human rights advocates about the poor conditions and violence inside the hotel, and that they are haunted by flashbacks and terrified they will be retaliated against next.
Human rights advocates and experts have warned for months that conditions at the Hotel Bamy – a run-down establishment that has served as a detention center for US deportees – are dangerous.
The US has sent at least 66 people from different African countries, Cuba and Brazil to Equatorial Guinea, which has received $7.5m as part of a deal to cooperate with the US deportation program. The Trump administration has pursued dozens of similar deals with countries to take in immigrants that the US cannot deport directly to their home countries, where judges have deemed they would face torture or persecution. In the past, the US government allowed those people to live and work in the US indefinitely.
The Trump administration, however, has sought instead to expel them to third countries where they have no ties, do not speak the local language and have no legal status – trapping them in limbo.
Advocates have been especially concerned for deportees sent to Equatorial Guinea, where the authoritarian government is notorious for human rights abuses, including torture, according to the US state department. Detainees held at Hotel Bamy have told the Guardian that armed guards keep watch over them 24/7, and that they have not been provided any medical care or even fresh clothes since arriving there. One of the detainees, who has a severe stomach hernia that requires visits to the hospital to drain his stomach due excessive fluid build-up, said he has been unable to see a doctor since arriving at Hotel Bamy.
Other detainees have managed to obtain medication for HIV, diabetes and other conditions via human rights lawyers, but remain fearful that access to medications will be arbitrarily cut off.
The two men who were tortured – Ahmed Soliman, 31, of Egypt, and Samson Birhane, 47, of Eritrea – have since been transferred to a prison in Malabo. Multiple witnesses recounted that the police officers shouted, “Where is the phone? Where is the phone!” as they beat the men, who had initially been accused of breaking a mirror at the hotel before they were pulled aside and arrested.
The beating, which occurred on 11 September, followed the release of a video first reported by Reuters showing conditions at the hotel and the violent behavior of the guards. The detainees had been using cellphones to communicate with lawyers and the media about the conditions they were facing.
In the video taken by Soliman, which lawyers shared with the Guardian, authorities are seen pointing guns at the deportees. A Cuban man asked the officer for the return of his confiscated mobile phone so he could contact relatives and a lawyer, but was ignored. When officers noticed Soliman filming the exchange with his mobile phone, multiple officers rushed at him and others standing nearby, pointed their guns, and told Soliman to remain on his knees with his hands up for 10-15 minutes.
In another video, Soliman was able to film authorities forcibly sending US deportees to Ethiopia, where they are likely to face torture. When deportees resisted going with authorities, officials gave them the option to “go back to their home country” or “go to prison”. At least 12 people have been returned by Equatorial Guinea to their home country, where they face persecution.
In May, human rights experts at the United Nations issued a rare public appeal asking Equatorial Guinea to halt plans to return deportees to their home countries and to comply with international human rights standards and avoid refoulement, or the expulsion of people to countries where they face persecution.
“This is a human rights catastrophe,” said Bella Mosselmans, director of the Global Strategic Litigation Council, who represents several of the deportees at Hotel Bamy. The US and Equatorial Guinea “must be held accountable for the atrocities they are committing”, she added.
In the week since Soliman and Birhane were beaten, police have also been searching the other detainees’ hotel rooms for cellphones, and have confiscated them. They have also barred lawyers from seeing the deportees. Authorities have told the 29 US deportees who remain at Hotel Bamy that they may never see Soliman or Birhane again, according to lawyers. One detainee who witnessed the beating said authorities treat them as if they are “blanks” who “don’t even exist”. Another detainee said an officer told her: “You will disappear from the earth. I am the law.”
Witnesses said they feared for the lives of Soliman and Birhane, who came to the US as children.
Soliman is a gay man from Egypt who had lived in Phoenix for most of his life. He had a green card, but lost status after he was convicted of drug possession. He served time for his crimes, and in October, a judge had determined he would face persecution and torture if he were to return to Egypt due to his sexuality.
Birhane had come to the US as a refugee when he was 13, but lost status after a conviction for robbery when he was in high school, in 1988. He was allowed to remain in the US after a judge ruled he faced torture in Eritrea, and had been regularly checking in with Immigration and Customs Enforcement as required.
Lawyers for the deportees shared copies of multiple emails they had sent to the US embassy in Equatorial Guinea alerting them to threats and violence against those detained at Hotel Bamy, but those messages have gone unanswered, they said. In July, amid a lawsuit challenging conditions for deportees, the African Commission issued an urgent interim order instructing the government of Equatorial Guinea to refrain from deporting, transferring, or relocating deportees against their will.
The US Department of Homeland Security did not respond to the Guardian’s request for comment.
A spokesperson for the state department said: “The US government will use all legal means to remove those with no right to remain in our country.”
The agency did not respond to questions about whether it was aware of how Equatorial Guinea was treating US deportees, nor would it acknowledge whether any measures have been taken to intervene.
“As a general matter, we do not comment on the details of our private diplomatic communications with other governments,” the spokesperson said.

Boks power & All Blacks of old - what did we learn from series?
- Published
South Africa further cemented themselves as the world's best team with a 3-1 victory over New Zealand in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series.
After losing the opening Test in Johannesburg, the world champions won three straight games, comfortably claiming the series with a 43-28 win in Baltimore.
The fourth Test, played in the United States, came after three Tests in South Africa where the All Blacks continued to show promising signs under Dave Rennie.
With the Rugby World Cup next year, what did we learn from the series, which replaced this year's Rugby Championship and will be played again in 2029?
Power remains Springboks' trump card
New Zealander Tony Brown's arrival as attack coach in 2024 pointed to South Africa's ambition to dominate in all facets of the game.
The former Highlanders head coach, who will join the All Blacks in 2028, is known for creating a cohesive attacking shape built on sharp ball movement.
But having been outscored in terms of tries over the first two Tests, the Springboks flipped their pack-power trump card - pivotal to their back-to-back World Cup successes - to prevent a repeat of New Zealand's victorious 1996 series win in South Africa.
Nothing illustrated that more than a monster maul that started just inside New Zealand's 22 and ended with Malcolm Marx peeling off to score the decisive try under the posts.
That came after a penalty try from a scrum in the first half. In Baltimore, their power again proved too much.
"South Africa have tried to play expansively a couple of times when we have dominance after hurting teams in the maul or scrum," Schalk Brits, a 2019 World Cup winner, told BBC Sport.
"New Zealand didn't have that dominance in the forwards, but people said they played beautiful rugby. I don't care if it is beautiful or not.
"Beauty is in the eye of the beholder and I love a maul and scrum."
Fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, who was injured at the end of May, returned to start all four Tests. He was initially named on the bench for the second match, only for Handre Pollard to withdraw.
Despite improving as the series went on, the 24-year-old lacked his usual flashes of individual brilliance.
It remains to be seen whether South Africa turn back to 32-year-old Pollard, as they did in 2023, on the biggest occasions to close out games.
Rassie Erasmus' experienced back-to-back World Cup winners - Marx (32), Eben Etzebeth (34), Pieter-Steph du Toit (34), Siya Kolisi (35), Damian de Allende (34), Cheslin Kolbe (32) - all remain regular starters.
The world champions have proven they can also play an exciting brand of attacking rugby, but appeasing the masses will not matter if a familiar formula can bring them three straight World Cups.
All Blacks return to what made them great
Scott Robertson's dismissal in January after two years as head coach sunk New Zealand to a new low.
Rennie, not the flashiest appointment, had to hit the ground running, and a stunning Test win over South Africa at Ellis Park was a case of doing just that.
The 33-16 victory injected jeopardy into a series which many had the Springboks winning comfortably, given their home advantage and recent dominance.
Hurricanes half-backs Cam Roigard and Ruben Love, both aged 25, were trusted by Rennie to instil a return to the All Blacks way - the ability to score from transition from anywhere on the field and compound scoreboard pressure.
Four or more tries in each Test in South Africa showed just that, with the third Test all square at half-time.
"Scott Robertson was a good culture coach but maybe not a brilliant technical coach. Dave Rennie is a brilliant technical coach," former England wing Ugo Monye told Rugby Union Weekly.
"After the Nations Championship, you could see the structures and how they want to play. I think the All Blacks' backline is the most skilled in World Rugby."
Love struggled to have the same commanding impact in Tests two and three, with fly-half Richie Mo'unga returning for the Baltimore game, his first Test since the World Cup final.
The 32-year-old Mo'unga, who is back after a stint in Japan, was not at the standard that made him one of the best fly-halves at the 2023 World Cup.
However, getting him back up to speed will be an All Blacks goal over the next 12 months.
Former England scrum-half Danny Care said: "Imagine what New Zealand would do with a platform and some dominance. It is great for the game that they are coming back to be the All Blacks of old, and the next 12 months will be fascinating."
World Cup rivals: France 'can play multiple styles', and be 'careful of Ireland'
South Africa live for must-win games. That is when, according to Brits, the Boks "come alive".
Defeat at Ellis Park cost them their world number one status - which was quickly regained - but also exposed a vulnerability.
South Africa, who lost matches in the pool stages of the past two World Cups, are currently the favourites to win next year's tournament in Australia, bringing a pressure they have not experienced previously.
"We hate being the favourite, we almost have to have our backs against the wall," Brits said.
"We prefer not to have the eyes on us and move under the radar. I think that is the best way for any team."
Back-to-back Six Nations champions France sent a weakened side to Christchurch in July and lost 34-32 to New Zealand.
When matched against the Springboks last November, France were beaten emphatically, 32-17.
Brits believes France are "the most settled" and offer tactical flexibility similar to that of the world champions.
"I feel like South Africa have an advantage as they can play multiple styles, and it feels like most other nations don't have that capability," Brits said.
"The only team that can play multiple styles is France, as they can grind it out with the forwards, play the kicking game and the expansive game as well."
He added that England still need to become what they are "supposed to be" and to keep an eye on Ireland, who are travelling "under the radar" after peaking in previous World Cup cycles prior to the tournament.
"Ireland still have amazing rugby players and coaches – the best coaches out there - and a top-four squad," Brits added. "Be careful of Ireland."

The 18th BRICS Summit was held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on 12–13 September 2026, with leaders from BRICS member and partner countries in attendance. In this context, a selfie purportedly showing Russian President Vladimir Putin, Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, and former Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi is being widely shared on social media (here, here). Let’s verify the claim made in the post.
Claim: A real selfie image featuring world leaders at the 2026 BRICS Summit.
Fact: The image is AI-generated. It includes individuals who did not attend the summit. The image also features former Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi, who died in a helicopter crash in May 2024. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
While reviewing the post, we noticed several inconsistencies in the viral image. The presidents of Brazil, the UAE, and Türkiye did not attend the 2026 BRICS Summit. Brazil was represented by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira, while Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan represented the UAE. The image also features former Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi, who died in a helicopter crash in May 2024. Therefore, the presence of these individuals in a purported selfie from the 2026 BRICS Summit raises questions about the authenticity of the image.
Additionally, we ran this image through AI detection tools. Hive Moderation showed this image was 99.9% AI-generated. Sightengine also showed it was 99% AI-generated.
Pictures of the leaders who participated in the conference can be seen here and here.
To sum up, this AI-generated image is being shared as a real photo of world leaders at the 2026 BRICS summit.
