In 2007, more than 20 African countries partnered up in a project to tackle desertification through the spread of the Sahara Desert, which was conceived as a giant wall of trees meant to stretch from coast to coast of the continent. Over time, the focus shifted to smaller-scale planting programs that go beyond just trees. The official goal for the length of the "wall" was 8,000 km. Today, however, reports show that the project has done poorly.
For several years, an image of a stretch of green trees across the African continent has spread online purportedly showing an ambitious inititative called the "Great Green Wall."
Such a plan has been in the works since 2007 and involves the participation of numerous African countries. Its aim was to have trees extend like a belt across the Sahel region, which is at the base of the Sahara, in order to prevent the expansion of the desert due to climate change.
According to social media posts on Facebook and other platforms, more than 20 African countries are a part of this effort to plant trees across the continent from coast to coast:
Across Africa, more than 20 countries are building something extraordinary together: the Great Green Wall. This massive belt of trees stretches from coast to coast along the southern edge of the Sahara, designed to stop the desert's spread and restore land that's been degraded for generations.
But here's what makes this different from other environmental projects. It's not just about planting trees—it's about restoring livelihoods for millions of farmers and communities who depend on this land. It's about fighting climate change by creating ecosystems that actually support people, not just preserve them behind barriers.
Imagine a living wall visible from space, built not to divide but to heal and unite an entire continent. That's the cultural shift we're witnessing: when nations choose collaboration over isolation, when environmental action becomes community action.
(Facebook user Culture Collective)
The posts are mostly true, in that this is a real effort being carried out by African countries, though the stated length of the wall upon completion varies. According to recent news coverage, the initiative is perceived as an overall failure with only small success stories.
According to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification, the project aimed "to restore Africa's degraded landscapes and transform millions of lives in one of the world's poorest regions, the Sahel. Once complete, the Wall will be the largest living structure on the planet – an 8,000 km natural wonder of the world stretching across the entire width of the continent."
The goal was to have the "wall" extend from Senegal in the west to Djibouti in the east, by 2030. The now-defunct official website of the Great Green Wall inititative detailed the reasons behind all their efforts:
The catalyst for the Great Green Wall is the daily impact of desertification and climate change that is undermining the futures of millions of communities across Africa's Sahel region.
Since the 1970s, the Sahel has been heavily affected by recurrent periods of drought. These droughts have threatened the livelihoods and future of entire populations across the region.
The lack of rain has led to the disappearance of livestock and the destruction of cereal crops. The great famines that rocked the Sub-Saharan region in the 80s each affected millions of people. In addition, the high population growth rate is increasing demand for food and pressure to gain access to other natural resources which are the basis for livelihoods and the survival of the rural population.
Millions of people – particularly rural youth – are currently facing an uncertain future due to the lack of decent rural jobs and continuous loss of livelihoods due to land degradation and falling yields.
But according to a 2021 Associated Press report, since the project's inception in 2007, millions of the planted trees have died due to diminishing rains and rising temperatures. Only 4% of the project's original goal has been met and around $43 billion is needed to complete it. Given these challenges, the focus of the project has shifted from planting just a wall of trees to a "mosaic" of smaller and more durable projects that emphasize community-focused solutions that support agriculture and prevent desertification.
The Great Green Wall's old website claimed a number of successes. Senegal planted around 12 million drought-resistant trees in less than a decade, while 5 million hectares of degraded land was restored in Nigeria, and 15 million hectares in Ethiopia. A November 2021 report in the journal Nature Sustainability assessed the economic effect of the program and concluded that it was economically worthwhile:
The Great Green Wall programme is a colossal initiative to restore 100 million hectares of degraded ecosystems across 11 countries in the region […] We evaluated the economic costs and benefits of future land restoration projects under this programme. We applied different scenarios that account for both market-priced and non-market benefits from restored ecosystems and consider the heterogeneity of local decision-making contexts in terms of investment planning horizons, discount rates, and the time needed for the restored ecosystems to start yielding their benefits in full. The results show that every US dollar invested into land restoration yields on average US$1.2 under the base scenario, ranging from US$1.1 to US$4.4 across the scenarios. At most, ten years are needed for land restoration activities to break even from the social perspective, accounting for both market-priced and non-market ecosystem benefits. To fund all proposed land restoration activities, an investment of US$44 billion is needed under the base scenario (US$18–70 billion across scenarios).
The report added that "violent conflicts in the Sahel are estimated to reduce the accessibility to these degraded ecosystems from 27.9 million hectares to 14.1 million hectares."
While originally only 11 countries were a part of the effort, more than 20 African nations have participated. This video from September 2020 detailed some of the projects and their effect:
A 2026 NPR report called the inititative a "cautionary tale" of poor planning and a lack of local participation. The report investigated 15 projects in Senegal, Djibouti and Chad, finding some more successful than others. A majority of the sites visited were unable to survive in the long term.

A silver medal can be a bittersweet achievement. It can mean you came second. Or, depending on how the competition unfolded, it can leave you wondering how close you came to winning gold.
There was perhaps a hint of that feeling in the first call Elavenil Valarivan immediately made after finishing second in the women’s 10m air rifle competition at the Nagoya Asian Games.
“I missed a gold! I was so close!” she told her coach, Neha Chavan, back in Chennai.
You could understand why she felt that way. The 27-year-old opened with a perfect 10.9 and led for much of the 24-shot final. She kept the Chinese shooters off the podium and pushed Olympic champion Ban Hyo-jin into third place. Gold had seemed within Elavenil’s grasp before a late stumble in the final three shots opened the door for Japan’s Hinata Taichi to move in front and win the title by 0.6 points, 253.0 to 252.4.
But Elavenil’s post-match call conveyed only part of how she felt. The rest is written in a scrapbook in which she makes a little note every time she shoots. But more on that in a while.
Elavenil’s medal is no ordinary silver.
You could see that in the beaming smile on her face as she held it up on the podium.
Follow | Asian Games Highlights, September 20
“I have a lot of gratitude. I’m trying to practise saying these words a lot more frequently and I’m just grateful I could win these medals,” she told Sportstar outside the Aichi Prefecture Shooting Range.
This was India’s first individual medal of the Nagoya Asian Games. It followed the team silver alongside Vidarsa Vinod and Sonam Maskar that Elavenil had helped secure in the qualification round earlier that morning.
More personally, both were the first medals Elavenil had won at a multi-sport Games.
“I’ve been competing at these multi-event Games for the last eight years. I’ve finally got my first medals,” she said.
When you look at her career, that statistic seems a strange sort of anomaly.
Ever since Olympic medallist Gagan Narang spotted her as a 14-year-old in Ahmedabad, there was a sense that Elavenil had something special. She has been competing internationally since 2018, when she was 18, and has since won medals at the Asian Championships, World Cups, World Cup Finals and World Championships.
She has also represented India at three major multi-sport Games — the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta, the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 and the Paris Games in 2024.
Yet she had never had a medal from one of them to show for it. At all three, she failed to make it beyond the qualification round.
There was more than enough time, then, for memories of those past disappointments to flood her mind during the one-and-a-half-hour drive from her team hotel in the port city of Nagoya, through winding hairpin bends and up into the hills towards the Shooting Range.
Instead, she looked out at the verdant mountainside and plugged in her earphones. Her playlist was a smorgasbord of Western rock, Punjabi belters, Bollywood hits and Tamil film classics.
“I’ve had a long journey from the time I first started competing. So when I got selected for these Asian Games, the first conversation I had with my coach Neha was that I had got my second opportunity to compete at an Asian Games eight years after my first. I was just grateful that I was getting the chance to be part of an Indian contingent and represent the country,” she said.
Before the competition, Elavenil had spoken to Neha, who has been part of her journey since she first picked up an air rifle 13 years ago.
“Neha just told me that I’d put in all the hard work already. She said, ‘You’ve trained your absolute best. Just trust your technique and be courageous,’” Elavenil recalled.
The first step was simply qualifying for the final. There was no guarantee that would happen.
After the first series of shooters had completed their qualification round, Elavenil knew she would need to be at her best not only to make the individual final but also to keep India in contention for a team medal.
At the start of her series, India trailed Japan by 0.7 points and Korea by 2.9 points in the team event. Those were the gaps Elavenil had to close.
Also read | Asian Games 2026 Medals Tally Live Tracker
She did so without missing a beat, shooting an unruffled 633.5 to qualify for the final and help ensure India finished ahead of both Japan and Korea.
That is why Elavenil’s emotions cannot simply be summed up by how she felt after the final.
Alongside the various odds and ends of equipment, snacks and kit in her shooting kitbag, Elavenil carries a small scrapbook to every competition. Once she has finished competing, she writes down how she thinks she has done. It is an immediate and honest assessment of her emotions, one she says she uses to get better in the future.
On Sunday morning, at the end of the qualification round in the women’s 10m air rifle competition, Elavenil fished it out and wrote down a single sentence.
“I did my best today.”

Late guilty plea halts trial over crash that killed weeks-old baby in WA's remote Midwest
In short:
Nathaniel Jackman has pleaded guilty to multiple charges relating to a ute rollover in the Midwest which killed a baby and two women in 2024.
His defence lawyer said Jackman had been forced to drive, despite not holding a licence.
What's next?
Jackman is due back in the Geraldton District Court for sentencing next year.
A last-minute guilty plea by the man behind the wheel has halted a trial over a ute rollover that killed a baby and two women in Western Australia's remote Midwest.
CONTENT WARNING: This story contains the names and images of people who have died.
Nathaniel Jackman was driving a Toyota Hilux, with five passengers on board, when it rolled on the Geraldton-Mt Magnet Road near Yalgoo, about 500 kilometres north of Perth, just before 11pm on August 10, 2024.
A weeks-old baby, Levi Ashwin, died at the scene from multiple injuries including skull and rib fractures, along with Gabrielle Brockman, 21, who suffered a head injury.
Levi's mother, 33-year-old Marrika Brockman, later died in hospital from a head injury.
Jackman, 24, had been due to face trial in the Geraldton District Court on Monday, but pleaded guilty to three counts of dangerous driving causing death, and two of dangerous driving causing grievous bodily harm.
The court heard Levi's father, Dwayne Ashwin, and another passenger, Jeffrey Incich, were seriously injured and would have died without medical intervention.
Prosecutors said Mr Incich was permanently disabled as a result, and now requires 24 hour support.
There was no infant car seat and the passengers were not wearing seatbelts.
No licence, drugs taken
The court heard the ute had travelled on the wrong side of the road and onto the verge for 70 metres before Jackman adjusted the wheel.
Prosecutors said Jackman had never held a licence, was driving tired and had too many passengers in the car at the time of the crash.
Police said blood pooling indicated four passengers were ejected at the start of the rollover.
A blood sample taken from Jackman tested positive for THC at the time of the crash, with the levels suggesting the then-22-year-old smoked cannabis the same afternoon.
'Forced' to drive, says lawyer
Defence lawyer George Guidice said Jackman had been forced to drive, despite saying he could not.
Mr Guidice said the group had travelled from Kalgoorlie to Meekatharra the day before the crash for a funeral.
He said there had been arguments after the funeral, with some of the group keen to stay another night, and others wanting to drive onward to Geraldton.
Mr Guidice said Dwayne Ashwin drove around 230 kilometres, past Mount Magnet, before telling Jackman to take over.
He said Jackman refused, but Mr Ashwin was "very forceful and insisted", adding that he become angry and started swearing.
Mr Guidice said Jackman then got behind the wheel as he "felt obligated" and that "he had a duty" to drive, despite never holding more than a learner's permit which had expired in 2022.
He said Jackman fell asleep while travelling at around 90 kilometres per hour.
"He woke up and he tried to steer the car onto the road," Mr Guidice said.
"He says he's very sorry for ever getting in the driver's seat … and accepts he should have never got in the driver's seat."
Mr Guidice said that Jackman was sorry for the pain he had caused the family of the three deceased.
He requested a pre-sentence psychological report, which the court heard could take 16 weeks.
Jackman's bail was extended with a $5,000 personal undertaking, a $2,500 surety, and conditions including reporting to police twice a week and providing urine samples.
He is due to appear before the District Court in Geraldton next February.

In September 2026, people shared various images online allegedly showing the moment immediately before an Israeli "double tap" airstrike reportedly killed a Gazan child who was attempting to help a wounded person. The images show one adult lying on the ground and the child, a boy, reacting to an incoming missile or other type of aerial weapon about to strike the ground.
A Snopes reader emailed an X post attachment, asking, "Very curious to understand if this picture posted to X is real. Stating it's a missile about to hit a child in Gaza."
(@mhdksafa via X)
A reverse image search found users sharing the same image (archived), as well as a slightly different image on Facebook (archived) and X (archived) — featuring differences in the appearance of the purported missile, debris from a destroyed building and a person lying on the ground.
(@PalPress24 via X)
The same reverse image search located posts of a third image showing the same scene, including on Instagram (archived) and X (archived) — also with differences in the appearance of the aerial object, the building debris and the person lying on the ground.
(@hasoonmasre via X)
In sum, the images provided a cropped and enhanced look at a real moment sourced from an authentic video, likely achieved with the help of artificial intelligence. One low-quality, blurry frame of that same genuine video, highlighted in other posts, truly appears to show a missile or other aerial weaponry right before a fiery explosion. For example, this post (archived) shows the authentic, unaltered moment:
(@Hakeam via X)
Two comparisons of the enhanced and original (blurry) frames confirm they were shot from the same perspective, ruling out the idea a photographer also separately captured a still picture at the exact same moment.
A Threads post hosts the authentic (and graphic) video. That post also displays one of the altered and enhanced images to the left of the genuine clip. The video itself doesn't display any signs of AI. The clip's one-minute length serves as a credible indicator of its authenticity (most AI-generated videos on social media are extremely short, lasting only seconds).
Snopes emailed the Israeli government (including the Israeli military) to pose questions about its purported participation in the airstrike. We also emailed the Pentagon, whose spokesperson referred us to the Israeli military, and emailed the White House, as well as news media outlets reporting out of Gaza, for comment. We will update this story if we receive further details.
More about the airstrike deaths
The Arabic-language Al Jazeera and Turkish state-run Anadolu Agency, as well as Palestinian outlets Al-Resalah and Shehab News Agency, all reported the news of the airstrikes.
Some of these outlets shared the enhanced images without making note of the alterations, reporting the location of the incident as the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood of Gaza City, the date as Sept. 15 and the identity of the young victim as Muhammad al-Zinati (الل محمد الزيناتي), a boy described as "no more than 15 years old" who was reportedly walking from a Quran memorization circle. According to the outlets, the video shows him approaching the man lying on the ground, identified as Sharif Shadi Labd (شريف شادي لبد), who was injured by an Israeli airstrike moments earlier.
The Shehab article and that publication's Telegram feed host other videos of al-Zinati's death, including clips reportedly showing his body covered in blood at the scene of the airstrike, as well as several moments with his father crying over him (longer video).
Getty Images hosts photos of the purported father, identified as a relative in several of the pictures, crying over a body, possibly al-Zinati. Its caption and other images match the neighborhood and date. The media-licensing company credited the pictures to photographers Ahmed Younis and Saeed M. M. T. Jaras.
Some of Shehab's still-image content appear to feature AI editing, for example the overly smooth look of an image showing the two victims posing together, possibly created from two authentic photos. The Al Jazeera (Palestine) Facebook page also featured (archived) one of the enhanced images, as well as other video clips allegedly from the same scene.
Via Messenger, we contacted Al-Resalah (archived) and Al Jazeera (Palestine) (archived) to inquire about the altered images in their Facebook posts, as well as Shehab News Agency via X to ask about another enhanced image in one of its posts (archived) — mainly whether the images were edited with AI or reposted from elsewhere. Al-Resalah and Shehab are both affiliated with the militant and political group Hamas, according to The New York Times and BBC News. We will update this article if we receive further information.
We found some of the aforementioned reporting by using Google Translate to search for the victims' Arabic-language names, a research strategy that can display results that may not show up in an English-only search.

The world is bracing for a “super” El Niño, and its effects are already being felt in India, where the monsoon has brought less rain than average but more intense downpours.
Meteorologists predict that the current El Niño, which is developing over the Pacific, could be one of the strongest in living memory. India is likely to be heavily affected, particularly later in the monsoon, when El Niño’s influence tends to strengthen.
But, as Ligin Joseph of the University of Southampton explains in The Conversation, its effects on India’s monsoon are not straightforward. A previous study in Science found that El Niño tends to bring more extreme summer monsoon rainfall to India.
This year, the southern state of Kerala has felt the brunt of the building super El Niño, with about a fifth less rain than normal. Yet intense downpours in the first week of August triggered flash flooding and landslides, killing 26 people.
The super El Niño is expected to peak after India’s monsoon season, but Indians are already keeping an anxious eye on the skies, wondering where and when the next deluge may come.

Rangers look like they know where they want to go - Celtic just look lost
- Published
At the end, every fibre of Derek McInnes' being must have wanted to have one of those Steven Gerrard moments, a scream of delight and relief into a Celtic Park camera lens, a human reaction to a significant victory on hostile terrain.
McInnes, though, showed little emotion. He shook hands with a now beleaguered Martin O'Neill and pretty much got out of there.
Later, the first words he uttered on radio were about not going "overboard" after back-to-back wins against their city rivals. "Just three points." he said. "Three points closer to Celtic."
That's true, of course, but it was also the first time a Rangers manager has won his first two games against Celtic since Graeme Souness in 1986. McInnes was 15 years old at the time.
So there was historical context but also deep relevance in the here and now. Rangers were good, and clearly deserving of the win, but they didn't quite hit the levels of ruthlessness of a week ago at Ibrox.
They can be better and yet they won as comfortably as it's possible to win when the margin at the end is just a single goal. Their superiority would have been better reflected had they won by two.
O'Neill has problems mounting game-by-game
O'Neill said there was "not much between the sides" but nobody was really buying that, Celtic folk chief among them.
The Celtic manager has problems and they're mounting game-by-game. His team is physically weak and mentally substandard. They have lost the elan they had in a few games in early season. They were out-played, out-muscled and out-coached. Again.
O'Neill has time to pause now, time to reassess. Time, perhaps, to question whether he's got the answers to the myriad ills of his team.
He doesn't have robust players in midfield because his board has not delivered them. He doesn't have the kind of wingers the club had when Daizen Maeda, Liel Abada, the still unfit Jota and Nicolas Kuhn were knocking around.
In Yang Hyun-jun's absence - and week on week he appears to be spoken about as an absent world beater - James Forrest is the best winger they have. So says former captain Scott Brown, who knows Celtic players. Forrest is 35-years-old.
Neither does O'Neill, at present, have good instincts.
Starting Sebastian Tounekti at Ibrox last week was an odd call and he changed it at half-time. Going with Sam Johnstone in goal at Rangers back-fired.
Giving Luke McCowan his first start of the season on Sunday was another curious decision that didn't work. The midfielder was off the pace and never came out for the second half.
O'Neill's famed ability to problem-solve and inspire has deserted him, for now. When set against the newfound organisation and vigour of this Rangers set-up then Celtic look jaded.
Their supporters are being cast into a scenario that none of them want to be a part of - wondering aloud, or just quietly, if the icon still has it in him. He sounds like he does. If that is the case then he needs more from his assistants - or just better ones.
From board level to coaching and playing, the whole operation looks humdrum and in need of a mighty shake. It's as if the 5-1 Champions League disintegration against LASK has removed not just confidence but heart and soul.
There was little gumption at Ibrox in the 3-0 League Cup loss, there was only a brief early reaction against Ferencvaros in the Europa League before another beating, and now there's a third poor loss in a row and a fourth inside a month.
McInnes has really hit upon something
How quickly things turn. A few short weeks ago, as Rangers exited Europe to the sound of booing, McInnes didn't hold back when assessing the problems in his team.
Not a possession team, not a pressing team, not a counter-attacking team, he said. They were also too young and too inexperienced, a collection of individuals but not a unit - no identity, no discernible style of play.
What were weaknesses then are, in the blink of an eye, strengths now. Callowness has become youthful excellence.
For the second straight week, Olwethu Makhanya was the most dominant and classy defender on the pitch. He's 22.
For the second straight week the hardest-working and most effective attacking player was Ryan Naderi. He's 23.
Dan Neil and Nico Raskin, aged 24 and 25, were once again hugely influential in the middle of the park. Neil looked fairly ordinary not that long ago. Now he's growing fast as Rangers captain.
The oldest Rangers player from the start was James Penrice, who is 27. Celtic had six guys who were older than him in their team. The average age of the line-ups was 26.7 versus 24.4.
McInnes has moulded them all into a group of players who have, against Celtic, shown maturity and togetherness. He has really hit on something.
Certain things stood out. At half-time, Rangers were not just ahead thanks to Naderi's goal, they were winning battles all over the pitch, just as they had done last Sunday.
They were winning aerial duels by 67.6% to 32.4%, they had eight shots to Celtic's one, six on target to Celtic's zero.
Camilo Duran had eight touches of the ball, Kevin Kelsy had 13 and Naderi 23. All the individual match-ups were more or less Rangers victories.
Even when Celtic's club record-signing Kasper Hogh came on, not a lot changed. Rangers had more chances in the second half.
Hogh got no service again, but he's beginning to look like a player so devoid of belief that even if service did come his way there's no guarantee that he'd execute the way he did so often for Bodo-Glimt.
When your star striker can't get a start and when your leader, Callum McGregor, is getting over-run, then you have problems, too many for O'Neill to solve.
McInnes was right about the three points thing, but the momentum in Glasgow is his now. The energy, the clarity, the optimism is blue and not green. The power has switched with breakneck speed and, of course, it could switch back again if Celtic get their act together.
There are massive questions now, though. More than O'Neill would have ever faced in the city before.
Rangers look, at the moment, like a club that knows where it wants to go. Celtic, by contrast, look lost in a haze of confusion and uncertainty.

For years, the growl of a big, manly V8 engine had been fading from US auto assembly floors.
No longer.
A V8 is a gas engine with eight cylinders arranged in a V-shape. It has long been a go-to choice for Americans who want the power to tow, haul, or go very fast — though it generally uses way more fuel than smaller engines.
Now, even as gas prices rise, the V8 is getting a new lease on life. Washington has relaxed emissions rules, eliminated companywide fuel-efficiency fines, and ended the federal EV tax credit. Automakers are responding with new and revived V8-powered trucks and performance cars, betting that Americans' appetite for big vehicles still has plenty of runway.
Data suggests demand for big, gas-powered vehicles — particularly trucks — remains strong. According to Cox Automotive, US consumers spent about $15 billion on full-size pickup trucks in December alone.
"Consumers wanted these cars," Kevin Roberts, the director of market intelligence at CarGurus, told Business Insider. "It was just a challenging economic choice because of the regulations that previously existed. But there are different rules now."
America's V8 obsession
Detroit's Big Three are leading the way.
On Thursday, GM announced two new V8s for the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra. That's after the company invested roughly $830 million in US propulsion plants.
Ram Trucks brought back its Hemi V8 engine in August after discontinuing the motor just last year. This month, it relaunched the TRX, a V8-powered sport-oriented pickup the company markets as an automotive "apex predator."
Last May, General Motors stopped producing electric-vehicle batteries at its Western New York propulsion plant and restarted V8 engine production for trucks instead — a shift that required an $888 million investment.
Ford is making a different sort of V8 bet. The company's updated 2027 F-150 still offers the 5.0-liter V8, even as a turbocharged V6 replaces the outgoing four-cylinder as its base engine. The company also previously told Business Insider it plans to add a new, faster trim to its V8-powered Mustang Dark Horse lineup, called the SC.
The history of America's big engines
V8s are essential to American car-making culture.
First developed for US consumers in the early 1900s by Cadillac, V8s became synonymous with postwar expansion, cheap gasoline, and a domestic auto industry built around size and power. Ford helped popularize the engine in the 1930s, offering dramatic horsepower gains over smaller powertrains.
That popularity launched generations of American nostalgia.
"What customers actually want is more horsepower and more torque," said Dave Mann, a classic Ford Bronco owner and the president of motor oil company Performance Oil Technology. "That's where the money is, and that's the bread and butter for American automakers."
Sales dominance didn't last forever.
As fuel prices surged and emissions rules tightened in the 1970s and 1980s, consumer preferences shifted. Smaller, more efficient vehicles — many built by Japanese automakers like Toyota and Honda — surged in popularity. By the early 2000s, V8 engines, which had once powered more than half of all American vehicle sales, accounted for less than 20%.
The engine never disappeared. Instead, they just powered full-size trucks and enthusiast-minded racers.
"What makes V8s superior is the instant response when you hit the gas pedal," Justin Goldsberry, an enthusiast and author of the Automobile Innovations newsletter, previously told Business Insider. "Everything is immediate and highly responsive."
A big shift is on the horizon
Big trucks — including the best-selling Ford F-150 and second-best-selling Chevy Silverado — still remain wildly popular.
Those trucks have long been Detroit's best profit-makers. They've taken on new importance for car companies, especially as they announce billion-dollar write-downs after their EV transitions have gone slower than expected.
Whether they're reaching the market at the right time is an entirely different question.
As US pump prices keep rising, gas-saving mild hybrids, which pair electric motors with a standard gas-powered engine, are gaining popularity. JD Power told Business Insider that hybrids represented 15.9% of all vehicle sales in July, up 2.5% compared to the same month in 2025.
"We've seen a large increase in hybrids," Roberts said. "The US is starting to shake some of its gas-guzzler mindset."

Quick Answer
iOS 27 focuses on useful refinements, with better Liquid Glass controls, smarter Siri AI, natural-language Shortcuts, Safari web-change alerts, separate alarm volume, improved Photos tools, AirPods EQ, smarter password handling, and several everyday quality-of-life upgrades.
Apple has finally started rolling out iOS 27 to all eligible devices after testing it in beta for months. If you are reading this article, the update is already rolling out. If your iPhone supports it, you can go to Settings, General, Software Update, and update to the latest version.
iOS 27 isn’t a significant jump from what we have seen from iOS 18 to iOS 26. For those who are not aware, Apple has changed the version names to match the year. So instead of iOS 19, they moved it to iOS 26 to match the year 2026.
This year’s iOS 27 is more about refinement and fixing the issues that came along with iOS 26.
One of the biggest updates for most people, at least based on our insight, is the ability to refine the liquid glass design. Apple is now offering a separate setting to make your liquid glass look more frosted or transparent, and also allowing you to set different volumes for the alarms.
Plus, there is a new Siri and plenty of other Siri AI features, such as creating your own shortcuts using natural prompts. Let your password app fix compromised passwords, monitor website changes for free using Safari, and much more.
I have been testing iOS 27 for a few months now, testing its wide variety of features. In this guide, you will learn about the 27 best iOS 27 features that everybody should know and use for a better quality of life.
Table of Contents
Best iOS 27 Features You Should Know and Use
There are tens of new feature additions and improvements in iOS 27. However, not every new feature deserves your attention. There are a few features that really stood out for me and are genuinely useful in day-to-day life that everyone should be aware of. So here are my ten favorite picks before going to the comprehensive list of features.
Adjust Liquid Glass Design Transparency
It is evident that most people hated the new liquid glass design Apple introduced in iOS 26. Apple made the entire UI transparent overnight with a glossy effect, which made text hard to read and was resource-heavy.
Additionally, a few apps failed to adapt to this design perfectly, resulting in a bad user experience. However, Apple didn’t back off from the decision. Since the launch, Apple has continued to refine the liquid glass design to make it better and more usable.
In the latest iOS 27 update, Apple is offering a separate setting that lets you adjust the transparency of the liquid glass design. This setting is different from what we have covered in our TechPP videos, and here is how to use it.
Build Your Own Shortcuts Using Natural Prompts
Extensions and shortcuts are the two easiest ways to add missing features, whether it’s on your iPhone or in any browser. However, creating shortcuts isn’t always an easy task. It involves dealing with plenty of elements and actions, which can be hard for a casual user.
But that’s changing with iOS 27. The new Siri AI will now let you create a new shortcut based on simple, natural prompts. Now you can simply describe a shortcut using natural language, highlighting what it can do. For instance: A shortcut that automatically changes your iPhone wallpaper every morning or a shortcut that reminds you to drink water every two hours.
Since it uses AI behind the scenes, the possibilities are endless. You can describe whatever problem or feature you want to add through the shortcuts, and it will do it for you. However, the current implementation is not reliable for complex extensions. But it is a good start, and it will only get better in future versions.
I found using Claude or Codex to create iPhone shortcuts is the most reliable way, and it works much better for me than using Siri to create shortcuts, which often don’t get the desired results I wanted.
Let Your Password Apps Handle Your Compromised Passwords
When Apple first introduced the Passcodes app in iOS 18, it was super basic and missed a lot of the features found on other passcode management apps at the time. However, Apple continues to add new features, and the recent iOS 27 brings the ability to fix your compromised passwords automatically.
In simple words, if any of your passwords are compromised, your password app will automatically renew them into new passwords without you having to do it manually.
Password management apps are very good at finding your compromised passwords in data breaches. However, previously you had to manually visit every site and change the password yourself. But that’s going to change with iOS 27, where you can simply tap to auto-change the password, and it does it for you.
Monitor Any Web Changes in Real Time
This is my favorite addition to the Safari browser. Probably a feature that can kill many third-party apps. Apple has added a new Notify Me feature to the Safari web browser in iOS 27. It lets Siri AI monitor real-time changes on the website and notify you. Whether it’s an e-commerce price drop, real-time stock changes, or even a new article addition to any webpage, Safari can monitor it for you.
The best part is, you can describe what changes you want to get notified about in a natural prompt, and it does it for you. Also, there are no hard limits on how many trackers or websites you can track, and it lets you track changes every hour. Weekly, monthly, or even daily. The only requirement is that your device should support the Apple Intelligence feature.
Set Separate Volume for Your Alarms
Another feature that Apple should have introduced years ago is the ability to set custom volumes for your alarms in iOS 27. Previously, Apple used to have a single volume for all sounds, including alarms, calls, media, and notifications. In iOS 27, Apple is splitting that up, letting you set separate volume levels for alarms, media, and notifications.
One-Tap Access for Your Wi-Fi and Mobile Data Toggles
If you are someone who frequently adjusts the mobile and Wi-Fi toggles on your iPhone, iOS 27 is getting a very big, useful upgrade. Now, without needing to open the toggle or the entire panel, you can just individually turn your Wi-Fi toggle on and off directly from the toggle. It is enabled by default.
If you have customized it, you can just drag and drop the new network panel to get access to these features.
Auto-Paste Suggestions on Top of Your Keyboard
Another feature that Android users have enjoyed for years is now finally available on iPhone starting with iOS 27. Once you copy text or take a screenshot, the iOS keyboard now automatically suggests the recently copied clipboard text and images, which you can simply tap on and paste wherever you want.
Previously, it required you to long-press, select, and tap on the paste option to do that.
New Custom Equalizer for Your AirPods
Apple is rolling out a custom equalizer in the settings for AirPods. Now, iPhones with iOS 27 have a native AirPods equalizer in Settings to help you customize the audio output.
The new custom equalizer allows you to adjust lows, mids, and high frequencies separately. However, it is only available for devices running on H2 or later Pro devices, and for older devices, users need to rely on Apple’s Adaptive EQ.
Quickly View Photos Captured by You
One of the biggest downsides of iOS Photos is that the images captured from your iPhone are mixed with screenshots, memes, and other downloaded images saved from third-party apps. This makes it extremely hard for you to find the photos captured particularly from your iPhone. In iOS 27, Apple has added a new “Captured by Me” folder to the Photos app. It only shows the photos and videos taken with your iPhone camera, letting you easily find them.
Let Your Earbuds Automatically Pause When They Detect You Have Fallen Asleep
If you use AirPods, Apple has added another useful feature in iOS 27: your AirPods can automatically pause music, podcasts, or whatever you are listening to when they detect that you have fallen asleep.
Most apps these days offer sleep timers that automatically pause after a certain time. However, Apple’s implementation is more dynamic and doesn’t rely on a set time limit. Based on your movement, the AirPods automatically detect when you have fallen asleep and pause the music. This can be extra useful if you are someone like me who falls asleep, and it also eliminates the need for you to set a sleep timer every night.
The Phone App Automatically Shows Relevant Information While You Are on the Call
How many times have you searched for specific information during a call with a service agent? If your answer is often, then Apple has added a very useful feature for you.
With iOS 27, the Phone app on your iPhone now automatically shows relevant information when you are on a call in real time. These include your reservation numbers, order details, confirmation codes, and much more, which Apple can fetch from other Apple services. This eliminates the need for you to search through emails, messages, or other apps while speaking to customer support or during a business call.
Apple’s Mail App Is Now Better at Finding Information
If you use Apple Mail, it is getting a useful update. Starting with iOS 27, Apple says Mail search is upgraded to find more relevant information based on your search.
Now, instead of remembering the exact subject lines, names, or even words in your email, you can just use your natural tone and search for the exact information you want. Apple says the Mail app can now display more relevant information at the top of the search results, and it’s also smarter, as it can automatically identify the query and find the relevant information.
Now, You Can Set an Exact Expiry Time for Your Find My Sharing
If you use Apple’s Find My for location sharing, it is getting a useful update. You can select the exact time when your location sharing should stop. Previously, Apple only allowed you to share your location for an hour, until the end of the day, or until you manually turn it off.
But with iOS 27, Apple is giving you more flexibility, letting you choose a custom time. Now you can set a combination of days along with the hours to share your location. This also eliminates the need for you to manually remember to turn off location sharing if you have set it to indefinitely.
Now, You Can Turn Your Physical Cards Into Digital Passes
Apple Wallet app in iOS 27 lets you convert your physical cards into digital cards and store them in your Apple Wallet. Carrying a physical card can be a hassle, especially if you have multiple cards. It not only makes your wallet bulky, but also makes it hard to find the right one when you need it.
Moreover, there is a high chance that you can forget it, and it could get lost. Now, with the ability to convert your physical cards into digital ones, the Apple Wallet app eliminates all of these pain points. Plus, even if you want to carry a physical card, I would highly suggest converting it into a digital one, which can come in handy sometimes.
Improved AI Writing Tools Across the System
AI writing tools were the first Apple Intelligence features Apple introduced in iOS 18. However, Apple left them out and forgot to update them in iOS 26.
But in iOS 27, with the overall improvements in the AI features and getting close to what it has promised, Apple has also upgraded AI writing tools throughout the system.
Now, these writing tools are more advanced and improved. The best part of these AI writing tools is that they are integrated directly into the workflow.
So if you want to summarize, shorten, or fix spelling mistakes, you don’t need to switch apps. You can generate, rewrite, or correct text directly from your iPhone keyboard. Plus, Apple is also integrating these AI capabilities across the system, including Mail and the Notes app, letting you easily access them anywhere.
Easily Create Calendar Events Without Specific Details
Creating a calendar event requires you to fill in separate details for title, date, time, location, and other details. However, with iOS 27, Apple is making it easy for you to create or edit calendar events.
Now, without needing to fill everything manually, you can just create a calendar event using natural prompts.
For instance, you can ask Calendar to create a birthday event at 4 a.m. tomorrow, and it will do it for you. Calendar app can now understand details such as important keywords, dates (such as tomorrow at 4 PM), a person’s name, and other key details, and automatically create a calendar event. Plus, you can also edit using natural language.
Connect an iPhone Directly to Gym Equipment
If you own an iPhone and want to track your workout data, pairing it with an Apple Watch is the most sensible decision. However, it is expensive and can be overkill for users looking for basic fitness tracking features who don’t need distraction on their wrist.
However, the Apple Watch has this nifty feature where they connect to your gym equipment and receives live workout data, such as your speed, distance, pace, resistance, and the duration of your workout, which you can then measure and analyze in your Apple Health app.
If you do not own an Apple Watch or don’t want to carry it during your workout, Apple in iOS 27 has added the same GymKit functionality directly on your iPhone. So now your iPhone can directly connect to your compatible gym equipment and receive the live workout data. Plus, if you have an Acura Pro 3, you can also connect and track your real-time heart rate information.
Pause Location Sharing Without Disabling It Permanently
If you use Find My to share your location with others, iOS 27 is adding the ability to temporarily hide your location without permanently ending location sharing completely.
In previous versions, if you wanted to temporarily stop sharing your location, whether it’s because your iPhone battery is running out, or if you are planning a surprise, or if you don’t want to reveal your destination, you needed to permanently stop location sharing.
With iOS 27, you can temporarily hide your location from a person. The best part is that the person does not need to be removed, and you also do not need to remember to turn the location back on after the situation has ended.
New Improved Cleanup Tool for Your Photos
I personally hate AI photo editing features inside the Photos app. Recently, both Apple and Google have added several features that are designed to alter and convert your photos into AI-generated ones. However, one feature that I found very useful is the ability to remove unwanted people or objects from a photo directly in the Photos app without relying on third-party tools.
However, Apple’s initial version of the Clean Up Tool isn’t as great as expected. It struggled to remove unwanted distractions from an image. However, with iOS 27, Apple has significantly improved it. Now it’s on par with other clean-up tools that perfectly edit the image naturally, without leaving smudges or empty patches.
Automatically Organize Safari Tabs by Subject
With iOS 27, Apple’s Safari browser can now automatically organize tabs for you. Many other browsers have adopted this feature, but it took some time for Apple to implement it.
If you use the Safari browser and have many tabs open, you can enable the Auto-Organize feature so that it automatically organizes your tabs. This lets you easily find them or close all of them at once.
Generate Your Own Extensions for Safari
Similar to iOS Shortcuts, you can also generate your own extensions using natural prompts in Safari. If you have an Apple Intelligence-supported iPhone, you can just visit the extension tab and give it a natural prompt about what exact features the extension might have, and Apple Intelligence will create a fully working extension for you.
You can just use this extension for an individual web page, or for all the web pages in your Safari browser.
New Siri for Agentic Tasks
Apple is finally close to delivering the Siri it promised two years ago. With iOS 27, Apple is introducing the new Siri, called Siri AI, which is now better at answering your questions and also better at agentic tasks. Plus, it can now search across your Apple apps, including Mail, Messages, Photos, Notes, and all other supported apps, and get information for you.
You can create a reminder, edit a message, organize details, or complete another task. Plus, Siri can also have better context, which means it can remember the information that it gets from other apps. Although at its current stage it is not as advanced as Gemini or other intelligent or agentic AI tools, it is a good start for Apple to deliver what it promised.
It will only get better from now on. Plus, Siri is directly integrated into the system. You can activate it from any screen. Plus, it is free to use without any limitations, except for a few features that Apple might put behind a subscription paywall in the future.
New Wallpaper Extensions
If you customize your iPhone and set a new wallpaper often, this can come in handy. Apple is introducing a new wallpaper extension feature in iOS 27, which expands your wallpaper so it fits correctly based on your iPhone dimensions.
In most cases, if your iPhone wallpaper doesn’t match your iPhone screen dimensions, it can look blurry and pixelated. Plus, if you want to set it as a lock screen wallpaper, it can also affect the depth effect, making the overall wallpaper look blurry and clumsy.
With this new extension wallpaper, Apple now extends the wallpaper to perfectly fit your iPhone’s aspect ratio. The best part is it preserves the main subject and only generates the matching scenery at the image’s edges, so that the subject stays in the middle without being cut off.
Reply Inline to the Messages From Android Users
With the iOS 27 update, Apple is putting an end to another discussion of blue and green bubbles and Apple’s tactics to limit RCS messaging.
Apple iMessage now supports inline replies, where you can directly reply to a specific message sent from your Android friend. This is like a nested reply where you can long-press on any message and tap on Reply. Along with your reply, the other person’s message appears on top, making it easy for them to spot and understand.
New Siri Visual Intelligence
Siri is also now upgraded with better visual intelligence, and it is now live inside your camera app. Now you can spot objects inside your camera and ask Siri to describe them. This can be especially useful for visual intelligence tasks, such as translating the text from a photo, identifying a specific object or food, or extracting the details from a flyer.
Plus, the best part is that, since it is being done by Siri, you can also ask follow-up questions and even delegate tasks, such as adding the extracted information to your calendar or splitting and storing it in any app. Now, adjust your lock screen clock to make it look smaller.
This can be small, but useful for people who often customize their lock screen.
Apple is now letting you adjust the clock size on your iPhone lock screen. Now you can adjust the size of the lock screen clock even smaller. If you feel your clock is covering the important details of your wallpaper, or if you want it to take up less space, you can simply use the smaller clock feature to adjust its size and make it look smaller.
Organize Your Photos Better
While Apple’s Photos app search is smart enough to find the relevant image you are looking for using just natural prompts, Apple is also letting you add individual star ratings and keywords to the photos. Starting with iOS 27, you can rate the photos up to 5 stars and add keywords.
Photos app displays these details while you are browsing your media library, letting these photos stand out from the rest. This makes them easy to spot instead of manually comparing photos to find the best ones from your extensive media library.
Save Photos Directly From Videos
With iOS 27, Apple also introduced the ability to save any frame from a video. You can simply use the Save frame as a photo feature, and the video frame will be saved as a photo. You can save multiple frames as photos.
Here is how:
- Open the Photos app on your Phone
- Play any video and tap on the three-dot menu at the top
- From here, tap on the Save Video frame as a photo option
Get the Most Out of iOS 27
Those are the 27 best iOS 27 features that everyone should know and use.
Apple has officially started rolling out iOS 27. By the time we publish this post, the update is available for all eligible phones. You can update and test out these new features. Detailed videos of how to use the features are coming soon on our TechPP YouTube channel. If you have any issues or if you don’t find this feature on your iPhone, you can comment below. I am happy to help you.

Rakesh Trehan, popularly known as 'Raja D King', announced that his “iPhone Langar”, featuring free Apple iPhones, will take place on September 22.
Amritsar businessman and social media influencer Rakesh Trehan, popularly known as 'Raja D King', has made headlines after announcing plans to host an “iPhone Langar”, where around 100 iPhones will be given away for free. Trehan has previously gained attention for unconventional giveaways, including cash handouts and free petrol.
He announced that his “iPhone Langar”, featuring free Apple iPhones, will take place on September 22. He claimed "Jai Mata Di” had revealed the date and other details to him, and the distribution is scheduled between 12 pm and 2 pm.
Who is 'Raja D King'?
Popularly known as Raja D King, Trehan is an Amritsar-based businessman and social media personality who has grabbed attention for his giveaways.
Earlier, he launched ‘Petrol Langar’ in Chandigarh, offering free fuel to people at selected petrol pumps. Under the initiative, he announced fuel coupons worth ₹500 for owners of two- and three-wheelers, while four-wheeler owners were promised coupons worth ₹1,000.
His first attempt at distributing free petrol, however, led to overcrowding at the venue. Hundreds of people arrived, leading the police to intervene. Authorities later ordered the temporary closure of the petrol pump.
Trehan has described himself as a crypto trader and a former stock market investor. In an earlier interaction with media, he said he planned to give away 90 per cent of his wealth.
He said that he wanted to donate a large portion of the wealth he inherited from his father, along with 90 per cent of his personal wealth, news agency PTI reported.
Recently, Trehan distributed food supplies and ₹500 notes to several people in need in Chandigarh.
His giveaways have continued to attract attention, particularly since he uses the term “langar” to describe initiatives that go beyond the traditional practice of providing free food.
‘iPhone Langar’ in Chandigarh
Trehan described the upcoming giveaway as the result of years of personal devotion. "I remained absorbed in devotion. I gave up everything and everyone who was mine... I wanted to attain 'Jai Mata Di'; I wanted to know who 'Jai Mata Di' is, the source of everything we receive," he told news agency ANI.
He added that the September 22 event in Chandigarh would be the first in a series of such initiatives.
Reflecting on the response to his earlier giveaways, Trehan said the interest surrounding the iPhone distribution was different. "The curiosity I witnessed for iPhones, I’ve never seen anywhere else," he said.
He said people selected from Chandigarh and Mohali will receive the devices after their names are picked in a public draw.

Bharatiya Janata Party (MP) Nishikant Dubey said on Monday that he filed a defamation case against former finance secretary Subhash Garg. Dubey lambasted Garg for claiming that Dubey visited his office in 2018. "I have decided to correct this bad behaviour of Subhash Garg, former Finance Secretary. I have filed a case of criminal defamation against him because he has mentioned about meeting me in his office," Dubey said in a post on X. He added, "Subhash, for your information, since I became an MP in 2009, I have not visited the office of the Government of India, because in the protocol of the Government of India, the Secretary is below the MP." Dubey challenged Subhash Garg, saying, “...from 2009 till date, have I ever written any letter regarding transfer posting? Not only you, but if any of your friends also give me information regarding any of my letters or any office meeting, then I will consider you a man's son.” “For the man who ruined the country's economy, Subash, the only way is jail,” he added. The legal action by Nishikant Dubey follows a public feud sparked by Subhash Garg, who earlier questioned the official Q1 GDP growth data. In response to Garg's critiques, Dubey revived an old conflict by sharing a letter he had originally sent to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in March 2018. At the time, Garg was serving as the Secretary of the Department of Economic Affairs — a post he held before being elevated to Finance Secretary in March 2019. In the 2018 letter, Dubey had urged PM Modi to review Garg’s macroeconomic framework. He also took to X to recall his criticism of Garg. "I had written back in 2018 itself that the former Finance Secretary is ignorant. A person does not become wise from the pinnacle of foolishness," Dubey said in a post in Hindi. Later, on a podcast, Garg said the letter was dated March 2018 and that the transfer occurred in 2019. He accused Dubey of “blackmailing.” Garg alleged Dubey “came to him once in the office” to tell me to ask LIC chairman to do his work. “So, I asked him, ‘Why are you telling me this? LIC is not under my control’.” Garg claimed that the “work” Dubey was asking him to do concerned transfers and contracts. He said he refused to do his work. “No one takes his warnings seriously,” he added later. It was this comment by Garg that prompted Dubey to file a defamation case against him. Dubey rejected any suggestion that he had visited Garg's office during his tenure in government. Later, speaking with news agency ANI, Nishikant Dubey called Garg the “despicable” man. Investor sentiment towards new-age tech stocks remained divided this week, even as the broader Indian equity market continued to face pressure. Of the 64 stocks tracked by Inc42 until last week, 30 gained between 0.18% and 7.69%, while 34 declined by as much as 13.43%. Zappfresh was the biggest loser of the week. The stock fell to a record low of ₹54.02 yesterday before closing at ₹55.06, ending the week 13.43% lower. The decline came after CARE Ratings, on September 11 (Friday), flagged deviations of 10% to 25% in the use of proceeds from the company’s ₹59.06 Cr IPO. ESDS was the second-biggest loser, falling around 10% during the week to close at ₹1,545.15 after rallying sharply in the sessions following its listing. Kissht, ArisInfra, MobiKwik, ixigo, FirstCry, TAC Infosec, Paytm, and Eternal were among the other gainers this week. RentoMojo became the 65th stock in Inc42’s listed new-age tech universe following its stock market debut on Thursday (September 17). The company listed at a premium of nearly 19% to its IPO price and ended the week at ₹513.10, 6.9% above its listing price. With RentoMojo’s addition, the combined market capitalisation of the 65 new-age tech stocks stood at $170.2 Bn. Meanwhile, 360 ONE Asset CIO Sameer Nath retired from BlueStone’s board.
